yady udite bhāskare utpāṭyante tadā tāsāṃ pūjā kartavyā /
japāraktotpalaraktakaravīraraktacandanakuṅkumena gavyagomayena sapādahastabhūmiṃ saṃlipya tanmadhye caturasraṃ kārayet /
raktacandanakuṅkumābhyāṃ tanmadhye vartulaṃ vitastimātraṃ bhānuṃ pūjayet /
children.translated_text: When my task is accomplished, you shall depart from here. 'Oṃ hīṃ <s>Raktacāmuṇḍā</s> hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.' With this <s>mantra</s>, under <s>Puṣya</s> or <s>Hasta</s> <s>nakṣatra</s> (constellation), all herbs should be uprooted. Those men who dig, uproot, or gather herbs after the sun has risen—by the effect of the sun's rays drinking [their potency], their herbs become devoid of power. They do not produce <s>siddhi</s> (supernatural results). If they are uprooted after the sun has risen, then their worship must be performed. Having smeared the ground for a span and a quarter with cow dung, using <s>japā</s> (hibiscus), red lotus, red oleander, red sandalwood, and saffron, one should make a square in the middle. With red sandalwood and saffron, one should worship the sun in a circle of a span's measure in the middle.

children.text: pārśve candrādigrahān pūjayet /
children.translated_text: One should worship the moon and other planets on the sides.

children.text: tato raktabhaktapuṣparaktair vakṣyamāṇamantreṇa baliṃ dadyāt /
children.translated_text: Then one should give a <s>bali</s> (offering) with red food, flowers, and red [items] with the <s>mantra</s> to be stated.

children.text: uoṃ drāṃ drīṃ drūṃ draiṃ drauṃ draḥ saḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ drāṃ drīṃ drūṃ draiṃ drauṃ draḥ saḥ svāhā.'

children.text: anena mantreṇa pūjāṃ kṛtvotpāṭayed vīryayuktā bhavati sarvakāryakṣamā bhavati // UT_7.7
children.translated_text: Having performed worship with this <s>mantra</s> and then uprooting, [the herb] becomes endowed with potency and capable of accomplishing all tasks. // UT_7.7

body.translated_text: Especially employed in subjugation practices for humans. The one-leafed, combined with one's own bodily impurity, brings a woman under control. The two-leafed [brings] kings and royal servants [under control]. The three-leafed, combined with <s>śrī</s> (holy basil), greens, and pepper, brings a hostile army under control. The four-leafed, combined with a ball, brings a maddened rogue elephant under control. Now the procedure for uprooting is described: on a Saturday, having become pure, in the evening, having performed the twilight worship and other rites, having performed worship with the five offerings of fragrance, flowers, incense, lamp, and food-offering, holding unhusked grain and fruit in the hand, standing near the herb, one should recite the invocation. Then before sunrise, one should dig with a stick of <s>khadira</s> (catechu) wood. The <s>mantra</s> is: 'That by which <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (Viṣṇu), and <s>Maheśvara</s> (Śiva) dig you;

body.text:
Uḍḍāmareśvaratantra, Aṣṭamaḥ paṭalaḥ
athānyat sampravakṣyāmi nārīṇāṃ garbhadhāraṇam /

children.text: padmabījaṃ gavyapayasā saha yā narī pibati sā garbhavatī bhavati satyam eva ādityavāre nimantrayet candravāre bhakṣayet /
children.translated_text: A woman who drinks lotus seeds with cow's milk becomes pregnant—truly. One should invite [her] on Sunday and she should eat on Monday.

children.text: pūrvadigbhāgasthitaṃ śarīṣamūlaṃ gavyaghṛtena saha ṛtusamaye bhakṣayet sā saṃvatsareṇa garbhavatī bhavati /
children.translated_text: The root of the <s>śirīṣa</s> (mimosa) tree situated in the eastern direction, eaten with cow's ghee at the time of the fertile period—she becomes pregnant within a year.

children.text: anapatyā ca yā narī kapitthaṃ bhakṣayet sadā /
children.translated_text: And a woman who is childless should always eat <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple);

children.text: abhimantrya tu mantreṇa sāpi putravatī bhavet // UT_8.1
children.translated_text: having consecrated it with a <s>mantra</s>, she too becomes the mother of a son. // UT_8.1

children.text: ekavṛkṣataṭe nārī snānaṃ kṛtvābhimantrayet /
children.translated_text: A woman who bathes near a solitary tree and recites the <s>mantra</s>—

children.text: ādivandhyāpi deveśi bhaved garbhavatī hi sā // UT_8.2
children.translated_text: even one barren from birth, O lord of gods, she indeed becomes pregnant. // UT_8.2

children.text: devaḥ śivo bhaved yatra nadīsaṅgam asaṃnidhau /
children.translated_text: Where there is the god <s>Śiva</s>, near a river confluence,

children.text: tasyāṃ nadyāṃ diśi svāhā vandhyā putravatī bhavet // UT_8.3
children.translated_text: in that river, in that direction, <s>svāhā</s>—a barren woman becomes the mother of a son. // UT_8.3

children.text: vidhir atrocyate kapilāgomayenātha bhūmiṃ saṃlipya yatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: The procedure here is stated: having smeared the ground carefully with tawny cow's dung,

children.text: snātvā vidhiprakāreṇa maṇḍalaṃ kārayet tataḥ // UT_8.4
children.translated_text: having bathed according to the prescribed method, one should then draw a <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred diagram). // UT_8.4

children.text: caturasraṃ catuṣkoṇaṃ tanmadhye vartulaṃ smṛtam /
children.translated_text: A square with four corners; in its middle, a circle is prescribed;

children.text: tanmadhye vilikhet paścād aṣṭapattraṃ sakarṇikam // UT_8.5
children.translated_text: in its middle one should then draw an eight-petaled [lotus] with a pericarp. // UT_8.5

children.text: madhye tu pūjayed devaṃ pattre śaktiṃ prapūjayet /
children.translated_text: In the center one should worship the deity; on the petals one should worship <s>Śakti</s> (the divine feminine power).

children.text: nirvraṇamaṇḍalasyāgre kamalaṃ sthāpayed budhaḥ // UT_8.6
children.translated_text: The wise one should place a lotus at the front of the unblemished <s>maṇḍala</s>. // UT_8.6

children.text:
śikhipattranakhavarṇena likhet /
bhṛṅgatā kulasaptaparvatamṛttikā [... au5 Zeichenjh] svamalāmṛttikāvalmīkamṛttikānimbamūlamṛttikā suvarṇarajatatāmrakāṃsyasahasramūlasarvatīrthāni samudrāḥ saritaḥ sarvāḥ sarvauṣadhayaḥ sarvadevatāḥ sarvasiddhayaḥ sarvayoginyaḥ sarve girayaḥ sarve nāgāḥ pañcajātyāni phalāni pañcaprakārākṣatāni pañca suvarṇapuṣpāṇi sthiracittena mantritakalaśe parikalpayet /
children.translated_text: One should draw with peacock feather and nail-pigment. [The ingredients:] <s>bhṛṅga</s> (a plant), earth from the seven family mountains, [...] earth from one's own impurity, anthill earth, earth from the root of the <s>nīmba</s> (neem) tree, gold, silver, copper, bronze, a thousand roots, all sacred bathing places, oceans, all rivers, all herbs, all deities, all <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers), all <s>yoginīs</s>, all mountains, all <s>nāgas</s> (serpents), fruits of five kinds, five types of unhusked grain, five golden flowers—one should arrange [all these] in the consecrated water-vessel with steady mind.

children.text: atha mantraḥ kṣaṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣaiṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now the <s>mantra</s>: 'Kṣaṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣaiṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ.'

children.text: anena mantreṇa yā narī vidhānena niratavarjitā abrahmacāriṇī devī vandhyā pañcapativarjitā /
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, a woman who is [performed upon] according to the rite, free from prohibition, not observing <s>brahmacarya</s>, O goddess—a barren woman, excluding one who has had five husbands—

children.text: aputrā labhate putrān durbhagā subhagā bhavet /
children.translated_text: a childless woman obtains sons; an unfortunate one becomes fortunate.

children.text: anenaiva vidhānena kanyā prāpnoti satpatim // UT_8.7
children.translated_text: By this very procedure, a maiden obtains a good husband. // UT_8.7

children.text: mantrauṣadhīprayogāś ca ye cānye cūrṇakīrṇakāḥ /
children.translated_text: The applications of <s>mantras</s> and herbs, and whatever other powders and preparations—

children.text: navābhicāritāḥ kūrāḥ śuddhadehā bhavanti te // UT_8.8
children.translated_text: those who are not afflicted by the nine types of <s>abhicāra</s> (sorcery), of pure body, they become [successful]. // UT_8.8

children.text: ye cānye vighnakartāraś caranti bhuvi rākṣasāḥ /
children.translated_text: And whatever other obstacle-creating <s>Rākṣasas</s> (demons) roam upon the earth,

children.text: te sarve pralayaṃ yānti satyaṃ devi mayoditam // UT_8.9
children.translated_text: they all meet destruction—truly, O Goddess, [this is] spoken by me. // UT 8.9

children.text: sakṛd uccarite mantre mahāpuṇyaṃ prajāyate /
children.translated_text: By reciting the <s>mantra</s> even once, great merit arises;

children.text: brahmahatyādayo doṣāḥ kṣayaṃ yānti na saṃśayaḥ // UT_8.10
children.translated_text: sins such as <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing of a Brāhmaṇa) and others are destroyed—there is no doubt. // UT 8.10

children.text:
atha prathamopāya ucyate nāgakesara 10 māṣakaṃ gavyaghṛtena sahartusnānadivase pibet /
tadanantaraṃ bhartrā saha rātrau saṃyogaṃ kuryāt /
sā avaśyam eva garbhavatī bhavati /
atha dvitīyopāyaḥ śvetajīrakam 17 māṣamātrakaṃ rātrau mṛnmayapātre jalena saha nirāvaraṇasthāne samagrarātrau sthāpayet /
agnimadivase śilāyāṃ piṣṭvā paryuṣitajalena yā strī ṛtusnānadine pītvā rātrau bhartrā saha saṃyogaṃ kuryād avaśyaṃ sā garbhavatī bhavati /
atha tṛtīyopāya dakālvadmadīpi 10 māṣakaṃ gavyadugdhena saha yā ṛtusnānadivase pītvā rātrau bhartrā saha saṃyogaṃ kuryāt sā avaśyam eva garbhavatī bhavati /
iti tṛtīyopāyaḥ /
uoṃ ghaṇṭākarṇāya svāhā imaṃ saptadhā japtvā grāme nagare vā praviśet tatra viśiṣṭaṃ bhojanaṃ prāpnoti /
children.translated_text: Now the first method is described: one should drink 10 <s>māṣas</s> (a unit of weight) of <s>nāgakesara</s> (Mesua ferrea) with cow's ghee on the day of the menstrual bath. Then at night she should have union with her husband. She will certainly become pregnant. Now the second method: 17 <s>māṣas</s> of white cumin should be placed at night in an earthen pot with water in an uncovered place for the entire night. On a fire-day, having ground it on a stone, the woman who drinks it with the overnight water on the day of the menstrual bath and has union with her husband at night will certainly become pregnant. Now the third method: one should drink 10 <s>māṣas</s> of <s>dakālvadmadīpī</s> with cow's milk on the day of the menstrual bath and have union with her husband at night—she will certainly become pregnant. Thus the third method. [With the mantra] "<s>Oṃ Ghaṇṭākarṇāya svāhā</s>," having recited this seven times, one should enter a village or city—there one obtains distinguished food.

children.text: anyac ca bho alla me siddhā anenāṣṭottaraśataṃ japet /
children.translated_text: And another thing—O <s>Allā</s>, I have accomplished [this]; with this one should recite 108 times.

children.text: śirīṣamūlamṛdaḥ kṣetrasya catuṣkoṇeṣu mokṣayet tadā śaśakamūṣakavarāhacatuṣpādaprabhṛtīnāṃ mukhabandhanaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: One should release the earth from the root of <s>śirīṣa</s> (Albizia lebbeck) at the four corners of the field; then there will be binding of the mouths of hares, mice, boars, quadrupeds, and others.

children.text: adhunā sampravakṣyāmi mantrān me phaladāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Now I shall describe the <s>mantras</s> that are fruit-giving to me,

children.text: ye sidhyati daśānyūnaṃ mantrasādhanamuktidāḥ // UT_8.11
children.translated_text: which, when accomplished, grant liberation through <s>mantra</s> practice in no less than ten [days]. // UT 8.11

children.text:
śatrumitrodāsīnasādhyasiddhasya lakṣaṇam /
mantrākṣarāṇi likhitvā sādhakasya tasya yadāpi ca prathamavargākṣaro bhavati tadā mitraṃ dvitīyavargākṣaro bhavati tadā siddhaḥ /
tṛtīyavargasya yadā bhavati tadā sādhyaḥ caturthavargākṣaro bhavati tadodāsīnaḥ pañcamavargākṣaro yadā bhavati tadā śatrur jñātavyaḥ /
etān bhedān jñātvā mantraśodhanam ārabhet tadā sādhakānāṃ sukhāvaho bhavati atha kalpavṛkṣaṣaṇḍamūlāni yāni prakṣālitāni gavyadadhimiśritāyāṃ rājikāyāṃ saṃskāryāṇi /
tato niyamapūrvakaṃ bhakṣayet /
nirvyādhiyogeṣv amuṃ svamukhe niyojayet /
vidhānam asyā bravīmīti devī /
atha mantraḥ uoṃ namaḥ ṣaṇmukhāya śaktihastāya mayūravāhanāya auṣadhīkena dehi me bhava svāhā /
children.translated_text: The characteristics of determining enemy, friend, neutral, to-be-accomplished, and accomplished [mantras]: having written the syllables of the <s>mantra</s> of the practitioner, when the first group of letters occurs, it is a friend; when the second group of letters occurs, it is accomplished; when it belongs to the third group, it is to-be-accomplished; when the fourth group of letters occurs, it is neutral; when the fifth group of letters occurs, it should be known as an enemy. Having understood these distinctions, one should begin the purification of the <s>mantra</s>—then it becomes conducive to the happiness of practitioners. Now the roots of the <s>kalpavṛkṣa</s> grove, having been washed, should be prepared with cow's curd mixed with mustard. Then one should eat them with [proper] observances. In conditions free from disease, one should apply it to one's own mouth. 'I shall describe the procedure for this,' says the Goddess. Now the <s>mantra</s>: "<s>Oṃ namaḥ Ṣaṇmukhāya śaktihastāya mayūravāhanāya auṣadhīkena dehi me bhava svāhā</s>" ("Oṃ, salutation to the Six-faced one [<s>Skanda</s>], who holds the spear, whose vehicle is the peacock—by medicine give to me, be [favorable], <s>svāhā</s>").

children.text: anena mantreṇa caturdaśyāṃ śucir bhūtvā mayūraśikhām utpāṭayet tadā mahāprabhāvayuktā bhavati /
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, on the fourteenth [lunar day], having become pure, one should pluck a peacock feather—then it becomes endowed with great power.

children.text: gavyaghṛtena saha saṃgṛhyeta tadā indriyabalo bhavati /
children.translated_text: When taken together with cow's ghee, one becomes strong in the senses.

children.text: pañcamalena svarṇakāro bhavati /
children.translated_text: With the five bodily substances (<s>pañcamala</s>), one becomes a goldsmith [i.e., achieves transmutation].

children.text: anyac ca śvetakaravīramūlaśvetagirikarṇikāmūlahevacanāṅbhīkṛtajātāñjalī pañcamalasamāyuktā khāne pāne pradātavyā maraṇāntaṃ vaśīkaraṇam // UT_8.12
children.translated_text: And another: the root of white <s>karavīra</s> (oleander), the root of white <s>girikarṇikā</s>, <s>hevacana</s> (a plant), <s>āṃbhīkṛtajātāñjalī</s>, combined with the five bodily substances—when given in food or drink, it produces subjugation unto death. // UT 8.12

children.text:
anyac ca śvetagirikarṇikāmūlaṃ svavīryeṇa saha svakīyapañcamalaharavīryaśvetārkamūlam etāni hastarkṣe puṣyarkṣe vā ekīkṛtya kumārikāhastābhyāṃ mardayitvā aṣṭamyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ vā gajamadena saha haste guṭikāṃ kārayet /
yasyai ekāpi dīyate sā vaśyā bhavati nānyathā /
śuklapakṣe 'pi sarpāṇāṃ dīyate te sarpā api vaśyā bhavanti śrīmahābhairavasya vaco yathā kuṅkumena saha dīyate tadā vai gajo vaśībhavati /
rocanayā kuṅkumena saha yadā tilakaṃ kriyate tadā sā strī pṛṣṭhalagnā bhramati /
gurudārebhyaḥ tilako na darśayitavyaḥ /
rājadvāre tathā nyāye vivāhe yuddhe jayāvahe trailokyamohanam etat /
triphalā 5 māṣāḥ nimba 1 māṣa kadamba 2 māṣa nīpa 3 māṣa tirāitā 4 māṣa karañja 5 māṣa bhṛṅgarāja 6 māṣa mayūraśikhā 7 māṣāḥ etāni samabhāgāni sūkṣmacūrṇāni kārayet /
tadanantaraṃ madhunā saha peṣayet /
bhojanaṃ ca yathāhāraṃ kurute nātra saṃśayaḥ /
etac cūrṇaṃ surebhyo 'pi durlabham /
children.translated_text: And another: the root of white <s>girikarṇikā</s>, together with one's own semen, one's own five bodily substances, the semen of <s>Hara</s> [a preparation], and the root of white <s>arka</s> (Calotropis)—having combined these under the <s>Hasta</s> or <s>Puṣya nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion), having ground them by the hands of a virgin, on the eighth or fourteenth [lunar day], with elephant musk, one should make a pill in the hand. She to whom even one is given becomes subjugated, not otherwise. Even when given to serpents in the bright fortnight, those serpents become subjugated—as spoken by the blessed <s>Mahābhairava</s>. When given with saffron, an elephant becomes subjugated. When a <s>tilaka</s> (forehead mark) is made with <s>gorocanā</s> (ox bile pigment) and saffron, that woman follows behind in a daze. The <s>tilaka</s> should not be shown to the wives of one's guru. At the royal gate, in legal disputes, at marriages, in battle—it brings victory; it enchants the three worlds. <s>Triphalā</s> 5 <s>māṣas</s>, <s>nimba</s> (neem) 1 <s>māṣa</s>, <s>kadamba</s> 2 <s>māṣas</s>, <s>nīpa</s> 3 <s>māṣas</s>, <s>tirāitā</s> 4 <s>māṣas</s>, <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia) 5 <s>māṣas</s>, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta alba) 6 <s>māṣas</s>, peacock feather 7 <s>māṣas</s>—these should be made into fine powder in equal parts. Then it should be ground with honey. One should eat food according to one's regular diet—there is no doubt. This powder is difficult to obtain even for the gods.

children.text: rātricūrṇaṃ śirīṣavalkalacūrṇaṃ ca gavyaghṛtena saha yasyai vanitāyai ṛtusnānadivase pānārthaṃ dīyate sā strī vandhyāpi garbhavatī bhavati nātra saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Night-powder and the powder of <s>śirīṣa</s> (Albizia) bark together with cow's ghee—when given to any woman for drinking on the day of her menstrual bath, that woman, even if barren, becomes pregnant—there is no doubt.

children.text: etac cūrṇaṃ kapitthaphalena saha ṛtusamaye aputravatī bhakṣayati sā strī putram āpnoti /
children.translated_text: This powder together with <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple) fruit, when a childless woman eats it at the time of her period, that woman obtains a son.

children.text: etac cūrṇaṃ śvetakaṅkolīmūlaṃ lakṣmaṇācūrṇaṃ ca samaṃ kṛtvā kuṅkumakvāthena sahartusamaye sadā bhakṣaṇārthaṃ dīyate tadā tasyāḥ śarīraśuddhir bhavati /
children.translated_text: Having made this powder, white <s>kaṅkolī</s> root, and <s>lakṣmaṇā</s> powder in equal parts, and when given for eating always at the time of the period with a decoction of saffron, then her body becomes purified.

children.text: paścād ṛtusamayopari pañca dināni bhakṣayet tadā sā garbhadhāraṇakṣamā bhavati nātra saṃśayaḥ // UT_8.13
children.translated_text: Afterward, she should eat for five days after the time of her period—then she becomes capable of bearing a child, there is no doubt. // UT 8.13

body.translated_text: <s>Uḍḍāmareśvaratantra</s>, Eighth Chapter. Now I shall declare another [topic]: the conception of children for women.

children.text: Uḍḍāmareśvaratantra, Navamaḥ paṭalaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Uḍḍāmareśvaratantra</s>, Ninth Chapter.

children.text: athānyat sampravakṣyāmi auṣadhaṃ paramadurlabham /
children.translated_text: Now I shall describe another medicine, supremely rare;

children.text: āsphoṭī nāma vikhyātā nāgadamanīti viśrutā // UT_9.1
children.translated_text: it is renowned as <s>āsphoṭī</s>, and well-known as <s>nāgadamanī</s> (serpent-subduer). // UT 9.1

children.text: asyā vidhānaṃ vakṣyāmi durlabhaṃ tridivaukasām /
children.translated_text: I shall describe its procedure, which is rare even for the celestials;

children.text: viṣāḥ sarve vinaśyanti lepanād bhakṣaṇāt kṣaṇāt // UT_9.2
children.translated_text: all poisons are destroyed by its application or consumption in an instant. // UT 9.2

body.text:
pattrahaste tāṃ pralipya sarpo dhriyate dhṛtamātre sarpo na naśyati naiva kṣatāni pralipya nāgapūjitamantreṇa sarpo vinaśyati /
nāgadamanīmūlaṃ khananān nāḍīlalāṭalepanān nāśayati samantataḥ āmavātaṃ pittavātaṃ śleṣmavātam ete vātā vinaśyanti bhakṣaṇān nātra saṃśayaḥ /
atha kathayāmy oṣadhīkaraṇe karaṇakāraṇāni /
putramaya vaśīkaraṇakārakaputraputraṃ kaṃsaṃ kātarāpi vaśaṃ paraṃ mahilājanasyaikaśa apy asya dīyate sā patiṃ parityajya paśyatāṃ lokānāṃ nagnā bhūtvā bhramati /
atha kathayāmi tāntrikavidhim /
tāmravedīparora iti lokair ucyate śanivāre tām abhimantrya digambaro muktakeśo bhūtvānudite bhānau grahaṇaṃ kuryāt /
piṣṭvā samyakprakāreṇa strīpañcamalena ca kāmātureṇa kṛtvā tāmbūlena saha bhaginīkṛtvā dīyate sā vaśyā bhavati nānyathā /
mātāpi putraṃ parityajya tatparā bhūtvā pṛṣṭhato nagnā bhavati yatra kutrāpi tathā tam anuyāti na saṃśayaḥ /
kākajaṅgheti vikhyātā mahauṣadhir grāme sarvatra tiṣṭhati śanivāre saṃdhyāsamaye tasyā abhimantraṇaṃ kuryāt tadantaraṃ brāhme muhūrte utthāyānudite bhānau puṣyarkṣe hastarkṣe vā yoge khadirakīlakena tāṃ samūlām utpāṭayet /
punas tāṃ saptamyām aṣṭamyāṃ navamyāṃ vā etāsu tithiṣu punarvasupuṣyahastarkṣayuktāsu svapañcamalena saha piṣṭvā svavīryaṃ svaraktam api tasmin dattvā yasyai vanitāyai dīyate sā strī vaśyā bhavati satyam eva mantreṇānena mantrayet /
uoṃ namo bhagavati tripure trailokyamohini aiṃ drāṃ śrīṃ klīṃ sauṃ amukanāmnīṃ śīghraṃ me vaśam ānaya svāhā /
iti mantraḥ /
atha guñjākalpo likhyate śvetaguñjāṃ śanivāre saṃdhyāsamaye 'bhimantritāṃ kṛtvā tato brāhme muhūrte utthāyānudite bhānau khadirakīlakena digambaro bhūtvā samūlām utpāṭayet /
puṣyarkṣe hastarkṣe vā strīpuṣpeṇa saha gorocanakaśmīrakuṅkumaśvetacandanaraktacandanakastūrīkarpūrahastimadena sahābhimantrya tilakaṃ kuryāt tadā strī kāmabāṇavimohitā vihvalā bhavati /

children.text: mantreṇānena mantrayet uoṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: One should consecrate with this <s>mantra</s>: "<s>Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>."

children.text: iti kāmabāṇatilakam /
children.translated_text: This is the <s>Kāmabāṇa tilaka</s> (Love-arrow forehead mark).

children.text: athānyatantroktaṃ vaśīkaraṇādikaṃ likhyate sāram uddhṛtya saṃkṣepād vaśīkaraṇamohane /
children.translated_text: Now the essence of subjugation and similar [practices] stated in another <s>tantra</s> is written, extracted in brief for subjugation and enchantment;

children.text: kāmināṃ prītijanakaṃ kiṃcit tad api gadyate // UT_9.3
children.translated_text: something that generates the affection of lovers is also described. // UT 9.3

children.text: tatrādau tilakavidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: First, the <s>tilaka</s> (forehead mark) procedure:

children.text: lajjāṃ madhūkaṃ kavyaṃ ca nalinīmūlam eva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Lajjā</s> (sensitive plant), <s>madhūka</s> (Madhuca), <s>kavya</s> (a plant), and the root of the lotus—

children.text: etān piṣṭvā svavīryeṇa yaḥ kuryāt tilakaṃ pumān // UT_9.4
children.translated_text: the man who, having ground these with his own semen, makes a <s>tilaka</s>— // UT 9.4

children.text: tatkṣaṇād eva nayati vaśyatāṃ bhuvanatrayam /
children.translated_text: at that very instant brings the three worlds under his control;

children.text: vātsyāyanena muninā proktaṃ yogam anuttamam // UT_9.5
children.translated_text: this supreme practice was taught by the sage <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. // UT 9.5

children.text: sitāṣṭamūlamañjiṣṭhā vacā mustā sakuṣṭhakā /
children.translated_text: <s>Sitāṣṭamūla</s> (eight white roots), <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder), <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag), <s>mustā</s> (nut grass), with <s>kuṣṭha</s> (costus)—

children.text: strīyoniśoṇite caitad ekīkṛtya lalāṭake // UT_9.6
children.translated_text: having combined these with the menstrual blood of a woman, on the forehead— // UT 9.6

children.text: śubhaṃ tilakam ādhatte yaḥ sa lokatrayaṃ kramāt /
children.translated_text: he who makes an auspicious <s>tilaka</s>, [subjugates] the three worlds gradually;

children.text: kṛtajñaḥ svavaśaṃ kuryān modate ca ciraṃ bhuvi // UT_9.7
children.translated_text: being grateful, he brings [all] under his own control and rejoices long upon the earth. // UT 9.7

children.text: tagaraṃ pippalīmūlaṃ meṣaśṛṅgī kaṇā jaṭā /
children.translated_text: <s>Tagara</s> (Indian valerian), root of <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper), <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s> (a plant), <s>kaṇā</s> (long pepper), <s>jaṭā</s> (spikenard)—

children.text: etat samaṃ svapañcāṅgamale nītvaikatāṃ sudhīḥ // UT_9.8
children.translated_text: the wise one should combine these equally with one's own five bodily substances; // UT 9.8

children.text: madhunā tilakaṃ kuryād yaḥ kṣoṇīsutavāsare /
children.translated_text: he who makes a <s>tilaka</s> with honey on Tuesday (the day of the son of Earth)—

children.text: jagat sarvaṃ vaśīkuryāt sa pumān nātra saṃśayaḥ // UT_9.9
children.translated_text: that man subjugates the entire world, there is no doubt. // UT 9.9

children.text: gorocanaṃ ca saṃbhāvya svapuṃso rudhireṇa yā /
children.translated_text: Having mixed <s>gorocanā</s> (ox bile pigment) with the blood of one's own male [organ],

children.text: kuryāt sā tilakaṃ bhāle patiṃ ca mohayed bhṛśam // UT_9.10
children.translated_text: the woman who makes a <s>tilaka</s> on her forehead greatly enchants her husband. // UT 9.10

children.text: athāñjanavidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Now the <s>añjana</s> (collyrium) procedure:

children.text: mahāṣṭamīdine yas tu śmaśāne naramastake /
children.translated_text: He who, on the day of <s>Mahāṣṭamī</s> (great eighth), on a human skull in a cremation ground,

children.text: pātitaṃ kajjalaṃ viśvaṃ mohayen nayanāñjanāt // UT_9.11
children.translated_text: collects the lampblack—[he] enchants the world by that eye-collyrium. // UT 9.11

children.text: rocanāṃ kesaraṃ kanyāṃ śilāṃ ceti viśodhayan /
children.translated_text: Purifying <s>gorocanā</s>, saffron, <s>kanyā</s> (aloe), and <s>śilā</s> (realgar)—

children.text: yājayed dṛṣṭipathagaṃ sarvam eva vimohayet // UT_9.12
children.translated_text: he who worships [with these] enchants everything that comes within the range of his sight. // UT 9.12

children.text: tālīśakuṣṭhanāgaraiḥ kṛtvā kṣoṇīśavartikām /
children.translated_text: Having made a wick with <s>tālīśa</s> (Flacourtia), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (costus), and <s>nāgara</s> (dry ginger) [mixed with] earth—

children.text: siddhārthataile niḥkṣipya kajjalaṃ naramastake // UT_9.13
children.translated_text: having placed it in mustard oil, [collecting] the lampblack on a human skull— // UT 9.13

children.text: pātayed añjanaṃ tasya sarvadā bhuvanatraye /
children.translated_text: he who applies that collyrium always [subjugates] the three worlds;

children.text: dṛṣṭigocaram āyātaḥ sarvo bhavati dāsavat // UT_9.14
children.translated_text: everyone who comes within the range of his sight becomes like a servant. // UT 9.14

children.text: śilākiñjalkaphalinī rocanānāṃ tathāñjanam /
children.translated_text: A collyrium of realgar, filaments [of lotus], <s>phalinī</s> (a plant), and <s>gorocanā</s>—

children.text: puṣyarkṣayoge vihitaṃ dampatyor mohanaṃ param // UT_9.15
children.translated_text: prepared under the conjunction of <s>Puṣya nakṣatra</s>, [is] the supreme enchantment for a couple. // UT 9.15

children.text: iti atha cūrṇavidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus. Now the powder procedure:

children.text: kākajaṅghā śilā pakṣau bhrāmarau kṛṣṇam utpalam /
children.translated_text: <s>Kākajaṅghā</s> (crow's leg plant), realgar, wings, bee, and black lotus,

children.text: tagarajaṃ caiṣāṃ cūrṇaṃ kṣiptaṃ vimohane // UT_9.16
children.translated_text: and <s>tagara</s> (valerian)—the powder of these, when thrown, causes enchantment. // UT 9.16

children.text: vātapaittikadalaṃ puṃso malaṃ mālāsavasya ca /
children.translated_text: Leaves of the wind-and-bile [type], a man's bodily substance, and <s>mālā</s> (garland) preparation—

children.text: pakṣāvaler idaṃ cūrṇaṃ kṣiptaṃ śirasi mohanam // UT_9.17
children.translated_text: this powder of [bird] wings, when thrown upon the head, causes enchantment. // UT 9.17

children.text: atha bhakṣaṇavidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Now the consumption procedure:

children.text: antrādi sarvaṃ niṣkāsya khañjarīṭodaraṃ kulaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having removed all the entrails from the belly of a <s>khañjarīṭa</s> (wagtail bird), with the ingredients

children.text: pūrayitvā svavīryeṇa sārameyagale kṣipet // UT_9.18
children.translated_text: filling it with one's own semen, one should place it around a dog's neck. // UT 9.18

children.text: mudrāṃ kṛtvā tadekānte saptāhaṃ dhārayet sudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: Having made a seal, the wise one should keep it in a secluded place for seven days;

children.text: paścān niṣkāsya saṃśodhya vaṭīṃ kuryād viśoṣayet // UT_9.19
children.translated_text: afterward, having removed and purified it, one should make a pill and dry it. // UT 9.19

children.text: sā bhakṣaṇavidhānena dīpamālā parasparam /
children.translated_text: That, by the consumption procedure, [shining] like a garland of lamps between each other,

children.text: dampatyoḥ prītijananī kīrtitā niyamottamā // UT_9.20
children.translated_text: is declared to generate affection between a couple—this is the supreme observance. // UT 9.20

children.text:
anyat sumatam /
athānyat sampravakṣyāmi tilakaṃ sarvakāmikam /
gorocanaṃ vaṃśalocanaṃ matsyapittaṃ kaśmīrakuṅkumakesarasvayambhūkusumasvavīryaśrīkhaṇḍaraktacandanakastūrīkarpūrakākajaṅghāmūlāni samabhāgāni kṛtvā kūpataḍāganadījalena mardayitvā kumārikāpārśvakāṃ guṭikāṃ kṛtvā chāyāṃ guṭikāṃ kārayet /
tayā lalāṭe tilakaṃ kṛtvā yāṃ yāṃ striyaṃ paśyati sā sā vaśyā bhavati /
drauṃ vāṃ dhāṃ kṣauṃ aṃ kaṃ chaḥ ity anena mantreṇa mahiṣāsthimayaṃ kīlakam ekonaviṃśatyaṅgulaṃ sahasreṇābhimantritaṃ yasya nāmnā kūpataṭe nikhanet sa mahiṣeṇa vadhyate /
uoṃ cchaḥ cchaḥ ḹṃ amukaṃ huṃ īṃ cchaḥ cchaḥ uoṃ iti /
anena mantreṇa mayūrāsthimayaṃ kīlakaṃ tryaṅgulaṃ sahasreṇābhimantritaṃ yasya nāmnā catuṣpathe nikhanet sa tatra bhramati /
tatrānenāvatiṣṭhati paryaṭati kṣaṇamātreṇa uttolanena śāntir bhavati /
children.translated_text: Another good method: Now I shall describe another <s>tilaka</s> for all desires. Having made <s>gorocanā</s> (ox bile), <s>vaṃśalocana</s> (bamboo manna), fish bile, Kashmiri saffron, <s>kesara</s> (saffron stamens), <s>svayambhūkusuma</s> (menstrual blood), one's own semen, sandalwood, red sandalwood, musk, camphor, and roots of <s>kākajaṅghā</s> in equal parts, having ground them with water from a well, tank, or river, having made a pill at the side of a virgin, one should dry the pill in shade. Having made a <s>tilaka</s> on the forehead with that, whatever woman one sees becomes subjugated. With the <s>mantra</s> "<s>drauṃ vāṃ dhāṃ kṣauṃ aṃ kaṃ chaḥ</s>," a peg made of buffalo bone, nineteen finger-lengths, consecrated a thousand times—when buried at the edge of a well in someone's name, that person is killed by a buffalo. "<s>Oṃ chaḥ chaḥ ḹṃ</s> [name] <s>huṃ īṃ chaḥ chaḥ oṃ</s>"—with this <s>mantra</s>, a peg made of peacock bone, three finger-lengths, consecrated a thousand times—when buried at a crossroads in someone's name, that person wanders there; remains there, roams about—but in an instant, by removal [of the peg], peace is restored.

children.text: uoṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ vrāṃ vrīṃ īṃ īṃ cchaḥ cchaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ vrāṃ vrīṃ īṃ īṃ chaḥ chaḥ svāhā</s>"—

children.text: anena mantreṇa meṣāsthimayaṃ kīlakaṃ dvādaśāṅgulaṃ sahasreṇābhimantritaṃ kṛtvā yasya gṛhe nikhanet sarvasiddhir asiddhā tasya bhavati /
children.translated_text: with this <s>mantra</s>, having made a peg of ram's bone, twelve finger-lengths, consecrated a thousand times, when buried in someone's house, all accomplishments become unaccomplished for that person.

children.text: drīṃ bandhūkapuṣpasaṃkāśaṃ dhyātavyaṃ mantradīpake /
children.translated_text: "<s>Drīṃ</s>"—one should meditate upon [a form] resembling a <s>bandhūka</s> (Pentapetes) flower, in the <s>mantra</s>-lamp;

children.text: kumbhakena varārohe śṛṇu vakṣyāmi ṣaḍguṇam // UT_9.21
children.translated_text: with <s>kumbhaka</s> (breath retention), O beautiful-hipped one, hear—I shall describe the sixfold [practice]. // UT 9.21

children.text: dhyātvā tu māsam ekaṃ tu mahāstrīm ānayed dhruvam /
children.translated_text: Having meditated for one month, one surely brings a great woman;

children.text: māsenaikena manunā ānayen nāgakanyakām // UT_9.22
children.translated_text: with this <s>mantra</s>, in one month, one brings a <s>Nāga</s> (serpent) maiden. // UT 9.22

children.text: devakanyāṃ tribhir māsaiḥ sāyāhne nānyathā bhavet /
children.translated_text: A divine maiden in three months, in the evening—it cannot be otherwise.

children.text: uoṃ haṃ haḥ iti /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ haṃ haḥ</s>"—

children.text: anenaiva tu mantreṇa dhyātavyāḥ krodhayājakāḥ // UT_9.23
children.translated_text: with this very <s>mantra</s> one should meditate upon those who perform anger-rituals. // UT 9.23

children.text: yājyasya rudrasaṃkāśaṃ rudrahastaṃ surāsuraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the one to be worshipped, [appearing] like <s>Rudra</s>, with the hand of <s>Rudra</s>, by gods and demons—

children.text: māsena mānuṣaṃ lokaṃ nāgalokaṃ dvimāsataḥ // UT_9.24
children.translated_text: in one month [one conquers] the human world, and the Nāga (serpent) world in two months; // UT 9.24

children.text: tribhir māsais tu deveśi svargalokaṃ na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: in three months, O Goddess of Gods, the heavenly world—there is no doubt;

children.text: ṣaṇmāsābhyāsayogena trailokyaṃ niścalaṃ kuru // UT_9.25
children.translated_text: by the practice of six months of <s>yoga</s>, one should make the three worlds motionless. // UT 9.25

children.text:
uoṃ raktahaṭā raktagaṭā mukuṭadhāriṇī edhati svāhā /
mantrarāja ulṭā vedhā /
uoṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ dhrīṃ vikṛtānanā bāhye phaṭ svāhā /
mantram imaṃ yantre likhitvā yasya īkṣitaṃ dīyate sa aikāhikadvyāhikatryāhikaviṣamajvareṇa gṛhyate tatkṣaṇād eva naśyati nātra saṃśayaḥ /
uoṃ bandhuna kṣayaṃ drīṃ drīṃ amukasyātmānaṃ nityajvareṇa pattrībandhanamātrasya sphura svāhā /
iti nityajvaraśodhanapattrikā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ raktahaṭā raktagaṭā mukuṭadhāriṇī edhati svāhā</s>"—[this is] the king of <s>mantras</s>, the reverse piercing. "<s>Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ dhrīṃ vikṛtānanā bāhye phaṭ svāhā</s>"—having written this <s>mantra</s> on a <s>yantra</s> (mystical diagram), when shown to someone, that person is seized by one-day, two-day, three-day, or irregular fever, [but] it is destroyed at that very instant—there is no doubt in this. "<s>Oṃ bandhuna kṣayaṃ drīṃ drīṃ</s> [name]'s self, by chronic fever, merely by binding the leaf, blaze forth, <s>svāhā</s>"—thus is the leaf-remedy for purifying chronic fever.

children.text: uoṃ kṣaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ kṣaḥ svāhā</s>"—

children.text: anena mantreṇa mantritaṃ jalaṃ bhṛśaṃ kṛtvā jvaritāṅgaṃ secayet tena jvaravimuktir bhavati niścitam /
children.translated_text: with this <s>mantra</s>, having thoroughly consecrated water, one should sprinkle it on the fever-afflicted limbs; by that, release from fever certainly occurs.

children.text: kharavāhanasiṃhasya kramād evānuśāsanam /
children.translated_text: The teaching, in order, of [<s>Śiva</s>] whose vehicle is a donkey and who is a lion—

children.text: ṛkṣaturagagato vāyur jīmūta iva garjitaḥ // UT_9.26
children.translated_text: the wind going through bears and horses, roaring like a thundercloud. // UT 9.26

children.text: ravivāre ślokam imaṃ likhitvā śirasi nyaset /
children.translated_text: Having written this verse on a Sunday, one should place it on the head;

children.text: tena sthāpitamātreṇa traimāsikajvaraṃ haret // UT_9.27
children.translated_text: merely by placing it, it removes a three-month fever. // UT 9.27

children.text: vāneyasya biḍālasya gṛhītvā rudhiraṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having taken the blood of a wild cat,

children.text: padmasūtrotthavartiṃ ca bhāvayet saptavārakam // UT_9.28
children.translated_text: one should prepare a wick from lotus fiber, [consecrating it] seven times. // UT 9.28

children.text: śivāgre tajjatailena pātayet kajjalaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Before [an image of] <s>Śiva</s>, one should collect lampblack with the oil produced from that;

children.text: tenāñjitalocanas tu adṛśyo bhavati dhruvam // UT_9.29
children.translated_text: one whose eyes are anointed with that surely becomes invisible. // UT 9.29

children.text: hebhirihebherihe /
children.translated_text: "<s>Hebhirihebherihe</s>"—

children.text: anenodakam ādāyālokya sahasravāraṃ parijapya anenaivāñjanena trirātreṇa siddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: with this [<s>mantra</s>], having taken water and gazing [at it], one should recite a thousand times; with this very collyrium, <s>siddhi</s> (success) is achieved in three nights.

children.text: padmasūtravartikasya tailena kajjalaṃ pātayet tenāñjitanetras tu adṛśyo bhavati /
children.translated_text: With the oil of a lotus-fiber wick, one should collect lampblack; one whose eyes are anointed with that becomes invisible.

children.text: tato gomūtreṇa cakṣuṣī prakṣālya punaḥ pratyakṣo bhavati // UT_9.30
children.translated_text: Then, having washed the eyes with cow's urine, one becomes visible again. // UT 9.30

children.text:
atha ḍākinīdamanamantraḥ akṣaḥ kṣāṃ kṣaukājasinau devatā tattvadhūlinī ghonāśālinī bhamantri bandhuśanādaivataṃ laghukaṇṭakena purum abhiśāsano devatāṃ mahābhairava maṇḍalam acala uoṃ cchaḥ cchaḥ cchaḥ ḍākinīmatabandhu namaḥ /
uoṃ namo bhagavate vajrāya caṇḍeśvarāya īṃ īṃ phaṭ svāhā /
iti sarvabhūtaḍākinīdamanamantraḥ /
children.translated_text: Now the <s>mantra</s> for subduing <s>Ḍākinīs</s>: "<s>Akṣaḥ kṣāṃ kṣaukājasinau</s>, the deity <s>Tattvadhūlinī Ghonāśālinī</s>, <s>bhamantri bandhuśanādaivataṃ laghukaṇṭakena</s>, subduing the city of the deity, O great <s>Bhairava</s>, the <s>maṇḍala</s> is immovable, <s>oṃ cchaḥ cchaḥ cchaḥ ḍākinīmatabandhu namaḥ</s>." "<s>Oṃ namo bhagavate vajrāya caṇḍeśvarāya īṃ īṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>"—thus is the <s>mantra</s> for subduing all <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits) and <s>ḍākinīs</s>.

children.text: damana sarpalaṅga ebhalisim ajabandhaniśi nāgapāśam acalaḥ iti damanamantraṃ bandhanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: "<s>Damana sarpalaṅga ebhalisim ajabandhaniśi nāgapāśam acalaḥ</s>"—thus is the subjugation <s>mantra</s> and the binding.

children.text: uoṃ raṃstrīṃ śīghraṃ ha svāhā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ raṃstrīṃ śīghraṃ ha svāhā</s>"—

children.text: tripurāṃ sindūraśaṅkhacūrṇābhyāṃ udanālapattre likhitvā śodhayitavyaḥ sa divasatrayeṇa jvareṇāgatya milati /
children.translated_text: having written <s>Tripurā</s> with vermilion and conch-shell powder on a lotus-stalk leaf, the [fever] should be purified; within three days the fever comes and meets [its end].

children.text: uoṃ ahohaḥ amukanamnīṃ śīghram ānaya svāhā ity ākarṣaṇam // UT_9.31
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ ahohaḥ</s> [name] bring quickly, <s>svāhā</s>"—thus is the attraction [rite]. // UT 9.31

children.text:
uoṃ strīṃ strīṃ valīṃ valīm īṃ ahaḥ phaṭ svāhā /
majjanasvastho bhavati /
apsaraṇīṃ amukīṃ jīva /
tena anena mantreṇa saptavāraṃ jalaṃ prajapya kāminyai pānārthaṃ dātavyam /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ strīṃ strīṃ valīṃ valīm īṃ ahaḥ phaṭ svāhā</s>"—one becomes healthy through bathing. [Saying] "O <s>Apsaras</s> [name], live!"—with this <s>mantra</s>, having consecrated water seven times, it should be given to the desired woman to drink.

children.text: uoṃ namo jale mohe kule phalāni saṃkule svāhā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ namo jale mohe kule phalāni saṃkule svāhā</s>"—

children.text: anena mantreṇa saptavārābhimantritaṃ yasya dīyate sa vaśyo bhavati /
children.translated_text: with this <s>mantra</s>, whatever is given [to someone] after being consecrated seven times, that person becomes subjugated.

children.text: uoṃ namo jale mohe drāṃ abjini phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ namo jale mohe drāṃ abjini phaṭ svāhā</s>"—

children.text: anena mantreṇa pratyūṣe pānīyena mukhaṃ prakṣālayet sarvajanapriyo bhavati sarvasiddhīśvaro bhavati // UT_9.32
children.translated_text: with this <s>mantra</s>, one who washes the face with water at dawn becomes dear to all people and becomes the lord of all <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments). // UT 9.32

children.text:
uoṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā /
tāmbūlaṃ mantrayitvā yasya dīyate sa vaśyo bhavati /
uoṃ namo jale mohe hana hana daha daha paca paca matha matha amukaṃ me vaśam ānaya svāhā /
atha yakṣiṇīmantrasādhanaṃ surasundarīmanohāriṇīkanakāvatīratikarīkāmeśvarīnaṭyanurāgiṇīpadminī etā aṣṭau yakṣiṇyaḥ kāmanāyāṃ sādhanam /
atha surasundarīsādhanam uoṃ hrīṃ āgaccha āgaccha surasundari svāhā /
vajrapāṇigṛhaṃ gatvā gugguladhūpaṃ dattvā trisaṃdhyaṃ pūjayet sahasraṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ māsaparyantaṃ japet tato māsābhyantare pratyakṣā bhavati antimadine raktacandanenārghyaṃ dadyāt /
tata āgatya mātā bhaginī bhāryā vā bhavati tāsāṃ yāni karmāṇi tāny eva karoti /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā</s>"—having consecrated betel with [this <s>mantra</s>], whoever it is given to becomes subjugated. "<s>Oṃ namo jale mohe hana hana daha daha paca paca matha matha</s> [name] bring under my control, <s>svāhā</s>." Now the <s>mantra</s> practice for <s>Yakṣiṇīs</s>: <s>Surasundarī</s>, <s>Manohāriṇī</s>, <s>Kanakāvatī</s>, <s>Ratikarī</s>, <s>Kāmeśvarī</s>, <s>Naṭī</s>, <s>Anurāgiṇī</s>, <s>Padminī</s>—these are the eight <s>Yakṣiṇīs</s>; [the following is] their practice for fulfillment of desires. Now the practice of <s>Surasundarī</s>: "<s>Oṃ hrīṃ āgaccha āgaccha surasundari svāhā</s>." Having gone to a temple of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, offering <s>guggula</s> (bdellium) incense, one should worship at the three <s>sandhyās</s> (junctions of day) and recite a thousand [times] at the three <s>sandhyās</s> for the duration of a month; then within the month she becomes visible. On the final day, one should offer <s>arghya</s> (oblation) with red sandalwood. Then, having come, she becomes a mother, sister, or wife; whatever tasks belong to those [roles], she performs exactly those.

children.text: yadi mātā bhavati tadā siddhadravyāṇi rasāyanāni dadāti /
children.translated_text: If she becomes a mother, then she gives <s>siddha</s> (perfected) substances and <s>rasāyanas</s> (elixirs).

children.text: yadi bhaginī bhavati tadā pūrvavad amūlyaṃ vastraṃ dadāti /
children.translated_text: If she becomes a sister, then as before, she gives invaluable garments.

children.text: yadi bhāryā bhavati tadā sarvam aiśvaryaṃ paripūrayati /
children.translated_text: If she becomes a wife, then she fulfills all prosperity.

children.text: paraṃ tu varjanīyam ihānyayā saha śayanaṃ sā ca maithunapriyā bhavati anyathā naśyati // UT_9.33
children.translated_text: However, one must avoid sleeping with another woman, for she is fond of intercourse; otherwise, she vanishes. // UT 9.33

children.text: atha manohāriṇīsādhanam uoṃ hīṃ āgaccha āgaccha manohari svāhā /
children.translated_text: Now the practice of <s>Manohāriṇī</s>: "<s>Oṃ hīṃ āgaccha āgaccha manohari svāhā</s>"—

children.text: iha nadīsaṃgame gatvā candanena maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā agurudhūpaṃ dattvā sahasraikaṃ mantraṃ māsaparyantaṃ pratyahaṃ japet /
children.translated_text: here, having gone to the confluence of rivers, having made a <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred diagram) with sandalwood, offering <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) incense, one should recite one thousand <s>mantras</s> daily for the duration of a month.

children.text: tato māsānte candanodakenārghyaṃ dadyāt puṣpaphalenaikacittena tasyā arcanaṃ kartavyaṃ tato 'rdharātrasamaye niyatam āgacchati āgatā satī tadājñāṃ karoti suvarṇaśataṃ tasmai sādhakāya pratyahaṃ dadāti // UT_9.34
children.translated_text: Then at the month's end, one should offer <s>arghya</s> (oblation) with sandalwood water, and one should perform worship of her with single-minded devotion using flowers and fruits; then at midnight she certainly comes. Having arrived, she carries out his commands and gives one hundred gold [coins] to that practitioner every day. // UT 9.34

children.text: atha kanakāvatīsādhanam uoṃ hrīṃ kanakāvati maithunapriye āgaccha āgaccha svāhā /
children.translated_text: Now the practice of <s>Kanakāvatī</s>: "<s>Oṃ hrīṃ kanakāvati maithunapriye āgaccha āgaccha svāhā</s>"—

children.text: vaṭavṛkṣasamīpe sthitvā madyamāṃsādinaivedyaṃ tasyai mūlamantreṇa dattvā śeṣaṃ svayam apy aṅgīkṛtya sahasram ekaṃ mūlamantraṃ japet /
children.translated_text: standing near a banyan tree, having offered food-offerings of wine, meat, and so on to her with the root <s>mantra</s>, and having accepted the remainder oneself, one should recite the root <s>mantra</s> one thousand times.

children.text: evaṃ saptadinaparyantaṃ kuryāt /
children.translated_text: Thus one should do for the duration of seven days.

children.text: aṣṭamyāṃ rātrāv ardharātrasamaye vastrālaṃkārabhūṣitā aṣṭau parivārān ādāyopagacchati /
children.translated_text: On the eighth night, at midnight, she approaches adorned with garments and ornaments, bringing eight attendants.

children.text: āgatā sā kāmayitavyā bhāryā vā bhavati dvādaśajanānāṃ vastrālaṃkārabhojanaṃ ca dadāti aṣṭau kalā nityaṃ sādhakāya prayacchati // UT_9.35
children.translated_text: Having arrived, she should be enjoyed; she becomes a wife and gives garments, ornaments, and food for twelve people, and bestows eight <s>kalās</s> (arts/portions) daily to the practitioner. // UT 9.35

children.text: atha kāmeśvarīsādhanam uoṃ hīṃ āgaccha āgaccha kāmeśvari svāhā /
children.translated_text: Now the practice of <s>Kāmeśvarī</s>: "<s>Oṃ hīṃ āgaccha āgaccha kāmeśvari svāhā</s>"—

children.text: iha gorocanayā bhūrjapattropari strīrūpāṃ pratimāṃ saṃlikhya ṣoḍaśopacāraiḥ pañcopacārair vā sampūjya tataḥ śayyāyām ekākī ekānte upaviśya tanmanā bhūtvā sahasraṃ japet tato māsānte tadbuddhyā svakīyāṃ bhāryāṃ pūjayet /
children.translated_text: here, having drawn the image of a woman on birch bark with <s>gorocanā</s> (ox bile pigment), having worshipped with sixteen or five <s>upacāras</s> (offerings), then sitting alone in solitude on a bed, having become absorbed in thought of her, one should recite a thousand times; then at the month's end, one should worship one's own wife with that intention.

children.text: tato madhusarpirbhyāṃ pratirātraṃ dīpaṃ prajvālya paścān maunaṃ kṛtvā mūlamantraṃ sahasrasaṃkhyaṃ japet /
children.translated_text: Then, having lit a lamp with honey and ghee every night, afterward maintaining silence, one should recite the root <s>mantra</s> a thousand times.

children.text: tato 'rdharātrasamaye niyatam āgacchati paraṃ tv anyāḥ striyo varjanīyāḥ // UT_9.36
children.translated_text: Then at midnight she certainly comes; however, other women must be avoided. // UT 9.36

children.text: atha ratipriyāsādhanam uoṃ hīṃ āgaccha āgaccha ratikari svāhā /
children.translated_text: Now the practice of <s>Ratipriyā</s>: "<s>Oṃ hīṃ āgaccha āgaccha ratikari svāhā</s>"—

children.text: atra paṭe citrarūpiṇī lekhyā vastrakanakālaṅkārabhūṣitā utpalahastā kumarī jātīpuṣpaiḥ prapūjanaṃ kuryāt guggulena dhūpaṃ dadyāt tato 'ṣṭasahasraṃ pratyahaṃ japet /
children.translated_text: here, on a cloth one should paint her in a beautiful form, adorned with garments, gold, and ornaments, holding a lotus. One should perform worship with <s>jātī</s> (jasmine) flowers and offer <s>guggula</s> (bdellium) incense, then recite eight thousand [times] daily.

children.text: māsānte tu vidhivat pūjanaṃ kuryāt /
children.translated_text: At the month's end, one should perform worship according to the prescribed rites.

children.text: dhūpadīpau prajvālanīyau tato 'rdharātrasamaye 'vaśyam āgacchati āgatā sā strībhāvena kāmayitavyā bhāryā bhavati sādhakasya parivāraṃ pālayati divyaṃ kāmikaṃ bhojanaṃ ca dadāti // UT_9.37
children.translated_text: Incense and lamp should be lit; then at midnight she certainly comes. Having arrived, she should be enjoyed as a woman; she becomes the practitioner's wife, protects his household, and gives divine, delightful food. // UT 9.37

children.text: atha padminīsādhanam uoṃ hīṃ āgaccha āgaccha padmini svāhā /
children.translated_text: Now the practice of <s>Padminī</s>: "<s>Oṃ hīṃ āgaccha āgaccha padmini svāhā</s>"—

children.text: svagṛhe candanena maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā śiraḥsthaṃ kārayet guggulena dhūpaṃ dattvā sahasram ekaṃ pratyahaṃ japet tato māsānte paurṇamāsyāṃ rātrau vidhivat pūjāṃ kṛtvā japet /
children.translated_text: in one's own home, having made a <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred diagram) with sandalwood, one should establish it at the head, offer <s>guggula</s> incense, and recite one thousand times daily; then at the month's end, on the full moon night, having performed worship according to rites, one should recite.

children.text: japānte 'rdharātrasamaye niyatam āgacchati āgatā sā kāmayitavyā bhāryā bhūtvā sarvakāmapradā bhavati rasaṃ rasāyanaṃ siddhadravyaṃ pratyahaṃ sādhakāya prayacchati // UT_9.38
children.translated_text: At the end of the recitation, at midnight, she certainly comes. Having arrived, she should be enjoyed; becoming a wife, she fulfills all desires, and gives <s>rasa</s> (mercury), <s>rasāyana</s> (elixir), and <s>siddha</s> (perfected) substances to the practitioner daily. // UT 9.38

children.text: atha naṭīsādhanam uoṃ hrīṃ āgaccha āgaccha naṭi svāhā /
children.translated_text: Now the practice of <s>Naṭī</s>: "<s>Oṃ hrīṃ āgaccha āgaccha naṭi svāhā</s>"—

children.text: atrāśokatale gatvā matsyamāṃsādyāhāragandhapuṣpādidhūpadīpabaliṃ dattvā sahasraṃ pratyahaṃ japet tataḥ sā māsānte niyatam āgacchati āgatā sā mātā bhaginī bhāryā vā bhavati /
children.translated_text: here, having gone under an <s>aśoka</s> tree, offering fish, meat, and other food along with fragrance, flowers, incense, lamp, and <s>bali</s> (offering), one should recite one thousand times daily; then at the month's end she certainly comes. Having arrived, she becomes a mother, sister, or wife.

children.text: yadi mātā bhavati tadā divyaṃ kāmikaṃ bhojanaṃ dadāti vastrasugandhisuvarṇaśataṃ dadāti ca /
children.translated_text: If she becomes a mother, then she gives divine, delightful food, garments, perfumes, and a hundred gold [coins].

children.text: yadi bhaginī bhavati tadā śatayojanād uttamāṃ striyam ānīya dadāti /
children.translated_text: If she becomes a sister, then she brings an excellent woman from a hundred <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) away and gives her.

children.text: yadi bhāryā bhavati tadā divyaṃ vastraṃ rasāyanam aṣṭadināntareṇa dadāti // UT_9.39
children.translated_text: If she becomes a wife, then she gives divine garments and <s>rasāyana</s> (elixir) every eight days. // UT 9.39

children.text: athānurāgiṇīsādhanam uoṃ hrīṃ anurāgiṇi āgaccha āgaccha svāhā /
children.translated_text: Now the practice of <s>Anurāgiṇī</s>: "<s>Oṃ hrīṃ anurāgiṇi āgaccha āgaccha svāhā</s>"—

children.text: iha kaśmīrakuṅkumena bhūrjapattre strīsadṛśīṃ pratimāṃ vilikhyāvāhanādikaṃ kṛtvā gandhapuṣpadhūpadīpādikaṃ dattvā tāmbūlāni nivedya sahasraṃ pratyahaṃ japet /
children.translated_text: here, having drawn an image resembling a woman on birch bark with Kashmiri saffron, having performed invocation and other rites, offering fragrance, flowers, incense, lamp, and so on, and presenting betel, one should recite one thousand times daily.

children.text: māsam ekaṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ japet māsānte paurṇamāsyāṃ vidhivat pūjāṃ kṛtvā ghṛtadīpaṃ prajvālya samagrarātrau mantraṃ prajapet /
children.translated_text: One should recite at the three <s>sandhyās</s> (junctions of day) for one month; at the month's end, on the full moon, having performed worship according to rites, lighting a ghee lamp, one should recite the <s>mantra</s> throughout the entire night.

children.text: tataḥ prabhātasamaye niyatam āgacchati āgatā sā sarvakāmapradā bhavati divyarasāyanāni dadāti pratyahaṃ ca dīnārāṇāṃ sahasraṃ dadāti /
children.translated_text: Then at dawn she certainly comes. Having arrived, she fulfills all desires, gives divine elixirs, and gives a thousand <s>dīnāras</s> (gold coins) daily.

children.text: tasyāḥ prasādena varṣasahasrāṇy āyuś ca bhavati // UT_9.40
children.translated_text: By her grace, one attains a lifespan of a thousand years. // UT 9.40

children.text: atha ṣaṭtriṃśad yakṣiṇyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now the thirty-six <s>Yakṣiṇīs</s>:

children.text: vicitrā vibhramā haṃsī bhīṣaṇī janarañjinī /
children.translated_text: <s>Vicitrā</s>, <s>Vibhramā</s>, <s>Haṃsī</s>, <s>Bhīṣaṇī</s>, <s>Janarañjinī</s>,

children.text: viśālā madanā ghaṇṭā kālakarṇī mahābhayā // UT_9.41
children.translated_text: <s>Viśālā</s>, <s>Madanā</s>, <s>Ghaṇṭā</s>, <s>Kālakarṇī</s>, <s>Mahābhayā</s>; // UT 9.41

children.text: māhendrī śaṅkhinī cāndrī śmaśānā vaṭayakṣiṇī /
children.translated_text: <s>Māhendrī</s>, <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>, <s>Cāndrī</s>, <s>Śmaśānā</s>, <s>Vaṭayakṣiṇī</s>,

children.text: mekhalā vikalā lakṣmīr mālinī śatapattrikā // UT_9.42
children.translated_text: <s>Mekhalā</s>, <s>Vikalā</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Mālinī</s>, <s>Śatapattrikā</s>; // UT 9.42

children.text: sulocanā suśobhāḍhyā kapālinī viśālinī /
children.translated_text: <s>Sulocanā</s>, <s>Suśobhāḍhyā</s>, <s>Kapālinī</s>, <s>Viśālinī</s>,

children.text: naṭī kāmeśvarī svarṇarekhā ca surasundarī // UT_9.43
children.translated_text: <s>Naṭī</s>, <s>Kāmeśvarī</s>, <s>Svarṇarekhā</s>, and <s>Surasundarī</s>; // UT 9.43

children.text: manoharā pramodānurāgiṇī nakhakeśikā /
children.translated_text: <s>Manoharā</s>, <s>Pramodā</s>, <s>Anurāgiṇī</s>, <s>Nakhakeśikā</s>,

children.text: bhāminī padminī caiva svarṇāvatī ratipriyā // UT_9.44
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāminī</s>, <s>Padminī</s>, and also <s>Svarṇāvatī</s>, <s>Ratipriyā</s>; // UT 9.44

children.text: ṣaṭtriṃśad etā yakṣiṇyaḥ kathitāḥ siddhikāmadāḥ /
children.translated_text: these thirty-six <s>Yakṣiṇīs</s> have been described, bestowers of desired <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments),

children.text: karaṅkiṇīmate tantre mahādevena vistarāt // UT_9.45
children.translated_text: in the <s>Karaṅkiṇīmata Tantra</s>, by <s>Mahādeva</s> in detail. // UT 9.45

children.text: ārādhanaṃ mahat tāsāṃ pravakṣyāmi samāsataḥ /
children.translated_text: I shall briefly describe the great worship of those [<s>Yakṣiṇīs</s>],

children.text: phalaṃ caiva yathā tuṣṭāḥ prayacchanti samāhitam // UT_9.46
children.translated_text: and also the fruits they bestow when pleased, with full attention. // UT 9.46

children.text: lakṣadvayaṃ japen mantraṃ vaṭavṛkṣatale śuciḥ /
children.translated_text: One should recite the <s>mantra</s> two hundred thousand times under a banyan tree, being pure;

children.text: paścāc campakapuṣpaiś ca homaṃ madhughṛtānvitam // UT_9.47
children.translated_text: afterward, [one should perform] a <s>homa</s> (fire oblation) with <s>campaka</s> flowers mixed with honey and ghee. // UT 9.47

children.text: kuryād daśāṃśato mantrī śaṃkareṇoditaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: The <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should perform [the <s>homa</s>] at one-tenth the count, as instructed by <s>Śaṅkara</s>;

children.text: tataḥ siddhā bhaved devi vicitrā vāñchitapradā // UT_9.48
children.translated_text: then <s>Vicitrā</s> becomes accomplished, O Goddess, and grants wishes. // UT 9.48

children.text: uoṃ vicitre citrarūpiṇi me siddhiṃ kuru 2 svāhā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ vicitre citrarūpiṇi</s>, grant me <s>siddhi</s>, grant <s>siddhi</s>, <s>svāhā</s>"—

children.text: iti mantraḥ /
children.translated_text: thus is the <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: lakṣadvayaṃ japen mantraṃ śmaśāne nibhṛte niśi /
children.translated_text: One should recite the <s>mantra</s> two hundred thousand times in a secluded cremation ground at night;

children.text: ghṛtāktair guggulair home daśāṃśena kṛte sati // UT_9.49
children.translated_text: when a <s>homa</s> is performed with ghee-anointed <s>guggula</s> (bdellium) at one-tenth the count— // UT 9.49

children.text: vibhramā toṣam āyāti pañcāśanmānuṣaiḥ samam /
children.translated_text: <s>Vibhramā</s> becomes pleased, equal to fifty humans;

children.text: dadāti bhojanaṃ dravyaṃ pratyahaṃ śaṃkaro 'bravīt // UT_9.50
children.translated_text: she gives food and wealth daily—so declared <s>Śaṅkara</s>. // UT 9.50

children.text: uoṃ hrīṃ vibhrame vibhramaṅgarūpe vibhramaṃ kuru 2 bhagavati svāhā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ hrīṃ vibhrame vibhramaṅgarūpe vibhramaṃ kuru kuru bhagavati svāhā</s>"—

children.text: pradeśe nagarasyātha lakṣasaṃkhyaṃ japen manum /
children.translated_text: in the outskirts of a city, one should recite the <s>mantra</s> one hundred thousand times;

children.text: padmapattrair ghṛtopetaiḥ kṛte home daśāṃśataḥ // UT_9.51
children.translated_text: when a <s>homa</s> is performed with lotus petals moistened with ghee at one-tenth the count— // UT 9.51

children.text: prayacchaty añjanaṃ haṃsī yena paśyati bhūnidhim /
children.translated_text: <s>Haṃsī</s> grants a collyrium by which one sees underground treasures;

children.text: sukhena taṃ ca gṛhṇāti na vighnaiḥ paribhūyate // UT_9.52
children.translated_text: one takes that with ease and is not obstructed by hindrances. // UT 9.52

children.text: uoṃ drīṃ namo haṃsi haṃsavāhinī klīṃ klīṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ drīṃ namo haṃsi haṃsavāhinī klīṃ klīṃ svāhā</s>"—

children.text: tripathastho japen mantraṃ lakṣasaṃkhyaṃ daśāṃśataḥ /
children.translated_text: standing at a three-way crossroads, one should recite the <s>mantra</s> one hundred thousand times, [performing <s>homa</s>] at one-tenth;

children.text: uoṃ śrīṃ drīṃ vaṭavāsini yakṣakulaprasūte vaṭayakṣiṇi ehy ehi svāhā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ śrīṃ drīṃ vaṭavāsini yakṣakulaprasūte vaṭayakṣiṇi ehy ehi svāhā</s>"—

children.text: madhūkavṛkṣatale mantraṃ caturdaśadināvadhi /
children.translated_text: under a <s>madhūka</s> (Mahua) tree, one should recite the <s>mantra</s> for fourteen days;

children.text: prajapen mekhalā tuṣṭā dadāty añjanam uttamam // UT_9.53
children.translated_text: <s>Mekhalā</s>, being pleased, gives the supreme collyrium. // UT 9.53

children.text: uoṃ drīṃ huṃ madanamekhalāyai madanaviḍambanāyai namaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ drīṃ huṃ madanamekhalāyai madanaviḍambanāyai namaḥ svāhā</s>"—

children.text: guhāntaḥstho 'dhare māsatrayaṃ mantraṃ japen naraḥ /
children.translated_text: a man standing inside a cave should recite the <s>mantra</s> facing downward for three months;

children.text: tataḥ siddhā bhaved devi vikalā vāñchitapradā // UT_9.54
children.translated_text: then <s>Vikalā</s> becomes accomplished, O Goddess, and grants wishes. // UT 9.54

children.text: oṃ vikale aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ vikale aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ svāhā</s>"—

children.text: svagṛhāvasthito raktaiḥ prasūnaiḥ karavīrajaiḥ /
children.translated_text: remaining in one's own home, with red <s>karavīra</s> (oleander) flowers,

children.text: lakṣam āvartayen mantrī dūrvājyābhyāṃ daśāṃśataḥ // UT_9.55
children.translated_text: the <s>mantrī</s> should recite one hundred thousand times, [performing <s>homa</s>] with <s>dūrvā</s> grass and ghee at one-tenth the count. // UT 9.55

children.text: home kṛte bhavet siddhā lakṣmīnamnī ca yakṣiṇī /
children.translated_text: When the <s>homa</s> is performed, the <s>Yakṣiṇī</s> named <s>Lakṣmī</s> becomes accomplished;

children.text: rasaṃ rasāyanaṃ divyaṃ nidhānaṃ ca prayacchati // UT_9.56
children.translated_text: she gives <s>rasa</s> (mercury), divine <s>rasāyana</s> (elixir), and [underground] treasure. // UT 9.56

children.text: uoṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ lakṣmi kamaladhāriṇi haṃsaḥ so 'haṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ lakṣmi kamaladhāriṇi haṃsaḥ so 'haṃ svāhā</s>"—

children.text: catuṣpathasthito lakṣam āpadi prajapen manum /
children.translated_text: standing at a four-way crossroads, in [times of] danger one should recite the <s>mantra</s> one hundred thousand times;

children.text: mālinī jāyate siddhā divyaṃ khaṅgaṃ prayacchati // UT_9.57
children.translated_text: <s>Mālinī</s> becomes accomplished and grants a divine sword, // UT 9.57

children.text: yat prabhāvena loke 'smin durlabhaṃ rājyam āpnuyāt /
children.translated_text: by whose power one may attain a kingdom difficult to obtain in this world.

children.text: uoṃ drīṃ uoṃ namo mālinī stri ehy ehi sundari haṃsahaṃsi samīhāṃ me saṅgabhaya svāhā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ drīṃ oṃ namo mālinī stri ehy ehi sundari haṃsahaṃsi samīhāṃ me saṅgabhaya svāhā</s>"—

children.text: śatapattravane yas tu mantralakṣaṃ japen muniḥ /
children.translated_text: the sage who recites the <s>mantra</s> one hundred thousand times in a grove of lotuses—

children.text: kṣīrājyahomaiḥ saṃsiddhā siddhiṃ yacchati bhūnidhim // UT_9.58
children.translated_text: when accomplished through <s>homa</s> with milk and ghee, [<s>Śatapattrikā</s>] grants <s>siddhi</s> and underground treasure. // UT 9.58

children.text: uoṃ drīṃ śatapattrike drīṃ drīṃ śrīṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Oṃ drīṃ śatapattrike drīṃ drīṃ śrīṃ svāhā</s>"—

children.text: nadītīrasthito lakṣatrayaṃ mantrī japen manum /
children.translated_text: Standing on a riverbank, the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should recite the <s>mantra</s> three hundred thousand times;

children.text: ghṛtahome daśāṃśena kṛte devī prasīdati // UT_9.59
children.translated_text: when a <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee) oblation of one-tenth is performed, the goddess becomes pleased. // UT 9.59

children.text: dadāti pādukāṃ tasmai yathāruci nabhastale /
children.translated_text: She gives <s>pādukās</s> (mystical sandals) to him, according to his desire, [for travel] in the sky;

children.text: manaḥpavanavegena yāti cāyāti sādhakaḥ // UT_9.60
children.translated_text: the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner) goes and comes with the speed of mind and wind. // UT 9.60

children.text: uoṃ drīṃ klīṃ sulocane siddhiṃ me dehi dehi svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Uoṃ drīṃ klīṃ Sulocane</s>, grant me, grant me <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment), <s>svāhā</s>.

children.text: raktāmbaradharo mantrī caturdaśadināvadhi /
children.translated_text: The <s>mantrī</s>, wearing red garments, for fourteen days,

children.text: japet siddhā bhaved devī śobhanā bhogadāyinī // UT_9.61
children.translated_text: should recite [the mantra]; the goddess <s>Śobhanā</s>, bestower of enjoyments, becomes accomplished. // UT 9.61

children.text: uoṃ drīṃ aśokapallavakaratale śobhane śrīṃ kṣaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Uoṃ drīṃ aśokapallavakaratale śobhane śrīṃ kṣaḥ svāhā</s>.

children.text: mahāvratadharo mantrī yaḥ śālyodanabhojanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>mantrī</s>, observing the great vow, eating [only] rice food,

children.text: lakṣadvayaṃ japen mantraṃ kapālaṃ labhate muniḥ // UT_9.62
children.translated_text: should recite the <s>mantra</s> two hundred thousand times; the sage obtains the <s>kapāla</s> (skull power). // UT 9.62

children.text: ākāśagamanaṃ dūrāt svapnarūpasamāgamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sky-travel, distant dream-form union,

children.text: dūrād darśanam ityādi sādhakāya prayacchati // UT_9.63
children.translated_text: distant vision and such—[the goddess] grants [these] to the <s>sādhaka</s>. // UT 9.63

children.text: uoṃ aiṃ kapālinī drāṃ drīṃ klāṃ klīṃ klūṃ klaiṃ klauṃ klaḥ haṃsaḥ so 'haṃ sakalahrīṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Uoṃ aiṃ kapālinī drāṃ drīṃ klāṃ klīṃ klūṃ klaiṃ klauṃ klaḥ haṃsaḥ so 'haṃ sakalahrīṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: sarittīre japen mantram ardhaṃ lakṣasya deśikaḥ /
children.translated_text: The preceptor should recite the <s>mantra</s> on a riverbank, half a <s>lakṣa</s> (fifty thousand times);

children.text: ghṛtāktaguggulair home devī saubhāgyadā bhavet // UT_9.64
children.translated_text: with oblation of ghee-soaked <s>guggula</s> (bdellium), the goddess becomes a bestower of good fortune. // UT 9.64

children.text: oṃ varayakṣiṇī varayakṣaviśālini āgaccha 2 priyaṃ me bhavatu haime bhava svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ varayakṣiṇī varayakṣaviśālini āgaccha āgaccha priyaṃ me bhavatu haime bhava svāhā</s>.

children.text: puṇyāśokatalaṃ gatvā candanena sumaṇḍalam /
children.translated_text: Going to a holy <s>aśoka</s> tree, [making] a fine <s>maṇḍala</s> with sandalwood,

children.text: kṛtvā cābhyarcayed devīṃ dhūpaṃ dattvā sahasrakam // UT_9.65
children.translated_text: having performed worship of the goddess, offering incense a thousand times, // UT 9.65

children.text: mantram ārādhayen māsaṃ naktaṃbhojī rasaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: one should propitiate the <s>mantra</s> for a month, eating only at night, always with <s>rasa</s> (juices);

children.text: rātrau pūjāṃ śubhāṃ kṛtvā japen mantraṃ munivrataḥ // UT_9.66
children.translated_text: having performed auspicious worship at night, one should recite the <s>mantra</s> with a sage's vow. // UT 9.66

children.text: naṭī devī samāgatya nidhānaṃ rasam añjanam /
children.translated_text: The goddess <s>Naṭī</s>, having arrived, [bestows] treasure, mercury, collyrium,

children.text: dadāti mantriṇe mantraṃ divyayogaṃ ca siddhidam // UT_9.67
children.translated_text: and gives to the <s>mantrī</s> a <s>mantra</s> and divine <s>yoga</s> that grants <s>siddhi</s>. // UT 9.67

children.text: uoṃ drīṃ naṭi mahānaṭi rūpavati drīṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Uoṃ drīṃ naṭi mahānaṭi rūpavati drīṃ svāhā</s>.

children.text: ekāsane śucau deśe trisaṃdhyaṃ trisahasrakam /
children.translated_text: On a single seat, in a pure place, three thousand [recitations] at the three junctions [of the day],

children.text: māsam ekaṃ japen mantraṃ tadā pūjāṃ samārabhet // UT_9.68
children.translated_text: one should recite the <s>mantra</s> for one month; then one should commence the worship. // UT 9.68

children.text: puṣpair dhūpaiś ca naivedyaiḥ pradīpair ghṛtapūritaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With flowers, incense, food offerings, and lamps filled with ghee,

children.text: rātrau devīṃ samabhyarcya japen mantraṃ prasannadhīḥ // UT_9.69
children.translated_text: having worshipped the goddess at night, one should recite the <s>mantra</s> with a serene mind. // UT 9.69

children.text: ardharātre gate devī samāgatya prayacchati /
children.translated_text: When midnight has passed, the goddess arrives and grants

children.text: rasaṃ rasāyanaṃ divyaṃ vastrālaṃkaraṇāni ca // UT_9.70
children.translated_text: divine <s>rasa</s> (mercury/elixir), <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenating elixir), garments, and ornaments. // UT 9.70

children.text: uoṃ hrīṃ āgaccha āgaccha kāmeśvari svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Uoṃ hrīṃ āgaccha āgaccha kāmeśvari svāhā</s>.

children.text: nadītīre śubhe ramye candanena sumaṇḍalam /
children.translated_text: On an auspicious and beautiful riverbank, [making] a fine <s>maṇḍala</s> with sandalwood,

children.text: vidhāya pūjayed devīṃ tato mantrāyutaṃ japet // UT_9.71
children.translated_text: having prepared [it], one should worship the goddess; then one should recite the <s>mantra</s> ten thousand times. // UT 9.71

children.text: ekaviṃśatighasrāntaṃ prasannā vitaret sadā /
children.translated_text: At the end of twenty-one thousand [recitations], she is always pleased and bestows [boons];

children.text: ardharātre gate devī dīnārāṇāṃ sahasrakam // UT_9.72
children.translated_text: when midnight has passed, the goddess [gives] a thousand <s>dīnāras</s> (gold coins). // UT 9.72

children.text: dadāti pratyahaṃ tasmai vyayaṃ kuryād dine dine /
children.translated_text: She gives [them] daily to him; one should spend [them] day by day;

children.text: tadvyayābhāvato bhūyo na dadāti prakupyati // UT_9.73
children.translated_text: due to the absence of that expenditure, she no longer gives and becomes angry. // UT 9.73

children.text: uoṃ hīṃ sarvakāmade manohare svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Uoṃ hīṃ sarvakāmade manohare svāhā</s>.

children.text: ardharātre samutthāya sahasraṃ prajapen manum /
children.translated_text: Rising at midnight, one should recite the <s>mantra</s> a thousand times;

children.text: māsam ekaṃ tato devī nidhiṃ darśayati dhruvam // UT_9.74
children.translated_text: after one month, the goddess surely reveals a treasure. // UT 9.74

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ pramodāyai svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ pramodāyai svāhā</s>.

children.text: kuṅkumena samālikhya bhūrje devīṃ sulakṣaṇām /
children.translated_text: Having drawn the goddess with auspicious marks on birch bark using saffron,

children.text: pratipattithim ārabhya dhūpadīpādibhir varām // UT_9.75
children.translated_text: beginning from the <s>pratipat tithi</s> (first lunar day), [worship] with incense, lamps, and other excellent [offerings]. // UT 9.75

children.text: kṛtvā devīṃ sahasraṃ ca trisaṃdhyaṃ parivartayet /
children.translated_text: Having made [the image of] the goddess, one should turn [the mantra] a thousand times at the three junctions;

children.text: māsam ekaṃ tataḥ pūjāṃ rātrau kṛtvā punar japet // UT_9.76
children.translated_text: for one month; then, having performed worship at night, one should recite again. // UT 9.76

children.text: ardharātre gate devī samāgatya prayacchati /
children.translated_text: When midnight has passed, the goddess arrives and grants

children.text: dīnārāṇāṃ sahasraikaṃ pratyahaṃ paritoṣitā // UT_9.77
children.translated_text: one thousand <s>dīnāras</s> daily, being pleased. // UT 9.77

children.text: uoṃ anurāgiṇi maithunapriye yakṣakulaprasūte svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Uoṃ anurāgiṇi maithunapriye yakṣakulaprasūte svāhā</s>.

children.text: gatvā pakṣigṛhaṃ mantrī nakhakeśaiḥ prapūjayet // UT_9.78
children.translated_text: The <s>mantrī</s>, going to a bird-house, should worship with nails and hair; // UT 9.78

children.text: dinaikaviṃśatir yāvat pūjāṃ kṛtvā tato niśi /
children.translated_text: for twenty-one days; having performed worship, then at night,

children.text: āvartayed ekacitto mantrī mantraṃ susaṃyataḥ // UT_9.79
children.translated_text: the <s>mantrī</s>, well-controlled and single-minded, should turn the <s>mantra</s>. // UT 9.79

children.text: niśārdhe vāñchitaṃ kāryaṃ devy āgatya prayacchati /
children.translated_text: At midnight, the goddess arrives and grants the desired task.

children.text: uoṃ hīṃ nakhakeśike svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Uoṃ hīṃ nakhakeśike svāhā</s>.

children.text: dinatrayam anāharī somasūryagrahe sati // UT_9.80
children.translated_text: Fasting for three days, during a solar or lunar eclipse, // UT 9.80

children.text: sparśād vimuktiparyantaṃ japet tadgatamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: one should recite with focused mind from the [beginning of] contact until the release;

children.text: tataḥ prasannā sā devī yacchaty añjanam uttamam // UT_9.81
children.translated_text: then, being pleased, that goddess grants the supreme <s>añjana</s> (collyrium). // UT 9.81

children.text: tenāñjito naro 'dṛśyaṃ nidhiṃ paśyati bhūgatam /
children.translated_text: Anointed with that, a man sees invisible treasure hidden underground.

children.text: uoṃ hīṃ yakṣiṇi bhāmini ratipriye svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Uoṃ hīṃ yakṣiṇi bhāmini ratipriye svāhā</s>.

children.text: vaṭavṛkṣatale kṛtvā candanena sumaṇḍalam // UT_9.82
children.translated_text: Under a banyan tree, having made a fine <s>maṇḍala</s> with sandalwood, // UT 9.82

children.text: yakṣiṇīṃ pūjayitvā tu naivedyam upadarśayet /
children.translated_text: having worshipped the <s>yakṣiṇī</s>, one should present the <s>naivedya</s> (food offering)—

children.text: śaśamāṃsaṃ ghṛtaṃ cīraṃ mantram āvartayet tataḥ // UT_9.83
children.translated_text: hare's flesh, ghee, and bark; then one should turn the <s>mantra</s>. // UT 9.83

children.text: dine dine sahasraikaṃ yāvat saptadinaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: One thousand daily, for seven days;

children.text: athāgatya sadā tasmai mantram añjanamuttamam // UT_9.84
children.translated_text: then she comes and always [gives] to him the <s>mantra</s> and the supreme <s>añjana</s> (collyrium). // UT 9.84

children.text: yatprabhāvāntare sarvaṃ paśyen nidhim aśaṅkitaḥ /
children.translated_text: By its power, one sees all treasures within [the earth] without fear.

children.text: uoṃ hrīṃ āgaccha 2 svarṇāvati svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Uoṃ hrīṃ āgaccha āgaccha svarṇāvati svāhā</s>.

children.text: śaṅkhaliptapaṭe yasmād devīṃ gaurīṃ dhṛtotpalām // UT_9.85
children.translated_text: On cloth smeared with conch-paste, one should [draw] the goddess <s>Gaurī</s> holding a lotus, // UT 9.85

children.text: sarvālaṃkāriṇīṃ divyāṃ samālikhyārcayen naraḥ /
children.translated_text: divine and adorned with all ornaments; a man should draw [her] and worship [her].

children.text: jātīpuṣpaiḥ prapūjyātha sahasraṃ parivartayet // UT_9.86
children.translated_text: Having worshipped with <s>jātī</s> (jasmine) flowers, one should turn [the mantra] a thousand times; // UT 9.86

children.text: saptāhaṃ mantravit tasyāḥ kuryād arcāṃ śubhāṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>mantra</s>-knower should perform her auspicious worship for seven days; then,

children.text: ardharātre gate devī samāgatya prayacchati // UT_9.87
children.translated_text: when midnight has passed, the goddess arrives and grants // UT 9.87

children.text: pañcaviṃśatidīnārān pratyahaṃ paritoṣitā /
children.translated_text: twenty-five <s>dīnāras</s> daily, being pleased;

children.text: vāñchitaṃ manasas tasmai mantrajñāya na saṃśayaḥ // UT_9.88
children.translated_text: [she gives] whatever is desired in the heart to the <s>mantra</s>-knower, without doubt. // UT 9.88

children.text: uoṃ uoṃ hīṃ ratipriye svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Uoṃ uoṃ hīṃ ratipriye svāhā</s>.

body.translated_text: Having applied it on the hand-leaf, a serpent is held—merely upon being held, the serpent does not perish; nor do wounds [when] anointed; but with the <s>nāgapūjita</s> mantra, the serpent is destroyed. The root of <s>nāgadamanī</s>, by digging and applying to the forehead and channels, destroys completely <s>āmavāta</s> (rheumatism), <s>pittavāta</s> (bile-wind disorder), and <s>śleṣmavāta</s> (phlegm-wind disorder)—these disorders are destroyed by consumption, there is no doubt. Now I describe the causes and methods in the preparation of medicines. [For] the subjugation of a son, the maker of subjugation—[even a] son, [even] <s>Kaṃsa</s>, [even] a coward becomes subject to the supreme [power]. Even when given to a single person among womankind, she abandons her husband and wanders naked before the eyes of the people. Now I describe the tantric procedure. What people call <s>tāmravedīparora</s>—on a Saturday, having consecrated it [with mantras], becoming sky-clad and with loose hair, one should collect it before sunrise. Having ground it properly with the five female substances, driven by desire, having offered it with betel as if making sisterhood, she to whom it is given becomes subjugated, not otherwise. Even a mother, abandoning her son, becoming devoted to him, follows behind naked wherever he goes—there is no doubt. The plant known as <s>kākajaṅghā</s> (crow's leg), a great medicine, grows everywhere in villages—on Saturday at twilight one should consecrate it with mantras; then at the <s>Brāhma muhūrta</s> (pre-dawn), having risen before sunrise, under <s>Puṣya</s> or <s>Hasta nakṣatra</s>, one should uproot it completely with a <s>khadira</s> (acacia) peg. Then on the seventh, eighth, or ninth [lunar day], on these <s>tithis</s> conjoined with <s>Punarvasu</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, or <s>Hasta nakṣatras</s>, having ground it with one's own five substances, adding one's own semen and blood—to whatever woman it is given, that woman becomes subjugated, truly. One should consecrate with this <s>mantra</s>: "<s>Oṃ namo Bhagavatī Tripure Trailokyamohini aiṃ drāṃ śrīṃ klīṃ sauṃ</s>, bring [name] quickly under my control, <s>svāhā</s>." This is the <s>mantra</s>. Now the procedure for <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus precatorius) is written: having consecrated white <s>guñjā</s> on Saturday at twilight, then rising at <s>Brāhma muhūrta</s>, before sunrise, becoming sky-clad, one should uproot it completely with a <s>khadira</s> peg. Under <s>Puṣya</s> or <s>Hasta nakṣatra</s>, having consecrated it with the menstrual blood of a woman together with <s>gorocanā</s>, Kashmiri saffron, white sandalwood, red sandalwood, musk, camphor, and elephant musk, one should make a <s>tilaka</s>—then the woman becomes bewildered, overcome by the arrows of <s>Kāma</s> (Love).

children.text: tatra ceṭakasādhanam /
children.translated_text: Therein, the <s>ceṭaka</s> (servant-spirit) practice.

children.text: atha ceṭakā likhyante /
children.translated_text: Now the <s>ceṭakas</s> (servant-spirits) are described.

children.text: kāmātureṇa cittena niśi mantraṃ japet sadā /
children.translated_text: With a mind burning with desire, one should always recite the <s>mantra</s> at night;

children.text: japto 'vaśyaṃ vaśyakaro mantro 'yaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ // UT_10.1
children.translated_text: when recited, this <s>mantra</s> surely brings [the target] under control—there is no doubt. // UT 10.1

children.text: oṃ aiṃ skīṃ klīṃ klīṃ sahavallari klīṃ kāmapiśāca klīṃ hrīṃ kāmapiśāca amukīṃ kāminīṃ kāmayāmy ahaṃ tāṃ kāmena grāhaya 2 svapne mama rūpe nakhair vidāraya 2 drāvaya 2 astreṇa bandhaya 2 śrīṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ aiṃ skīṃ klīṃ klīṃ sahavallari klīṃ kāmapiśāca klīṃ hrīṃ kāmapiśāca</s> [name] <s>kāminīṃ kāmayāmy ahaṃ tāṃ kāmena grāhaya grāhaya svapne mama rūpe nakhair vidāraya vidāraya drāvaya drāvaya astreṇa bandhaya bandhaya śrīṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: japen māsatrayaṃ mantraṃ kambalaḥ suprasannadhīḥ /
children.translated_text: One should recite the <s>mantra</s> for three months; <s>Kambala</s>, with a serene mind,

children.text: mṛtakotthāpanaṃ kuryāt pratimāṃ cālayet tathā // UT_10.2
children.translated_text: can raise the dead and also cause statues to move. // UT 10.2

children.text: sadāraktakambala mahādevadūta mṛtakam utthāpaya 2 pratimāṃ cālaya 2 parvatān kampaya 2 līlayā vilasaya 2 īṃ īṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Sadā-rakta-kambala mahādevadūta mṛtakam utthāpaya utthāpaya pratimāṃ cālaya cālaya parvatān kampaya kampaya līlayā vilasaya vilasaya īṃ īṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: caturlakṣaṃ japen mantraṃ sāgarasya taṭe śuciḥ /
children.translated_text: One should recite the <s>mantra</s> four hundred thousand times on the seashore, being pure;

children.text: pattrapuṣpaphalādīni karoty ākarṣaṇaṃ dhruvam // UT_10.3
children.translated_text: [with] leaves, flowers, fruits, and the like—it certainly causes attraction. // UT 10.3

children.text: abhaya ghudghutākarṣa karmakartā sṛṣṭiputra amukam ākarṣaya drīṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Abhaya ghudghutākarṣa karmakartā sṛṣṭiputra</s> [name] <s>ākarṣaya drīṃ</s>.

children.text: sahasrāṣṭam imaṃ mantraṃ japet saptadināvadhi /
children.translated_text: One should recite this <s>mantra</s> eight thousand times for seven days;

children.text: pratyahaṃ maṇibhadrākhyaḥ prayacchaty ekarūpyakam // UT_10.4
children.translated_text: daily, the one named <s>Maṇibhadra</s> gives one silver coin. // UT 10.4

children.text: oṃ namo maṇibhadrāya namaḥ pūrṇabhadrāya namo mahāyakṣāya senādhipataye mauddhamauddhadharāya sughaṭamudrāvahe svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ namo maṇibhadrāya namaḥ pūrṇabhadrāya namo mahāyakṣāya senādhipataye mauddha-mauddha-dharāya sughaṭa-mudrā-vahe svāhā</s>.

children.text: trisaṃdhyaṃ balidānaṃ ca niśāyāṃ prajapen manum /
children.translated_text: Offering <s>bali</s> (ritual offering) at the three junctions, one should recite the <s>mantra</s> at night,

children.text: sahasraṃ hi japen nityaṃ yāvat svapnaṃ prajāyate // UT_10.5
children.translated_text: a thousand daily, until a dream arises. // UT 10.5

children.text: prāṇināṃ mṛtyusamayaṃ vadaty eva na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: It tells the time of death of living beings, without doubt.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate rudrāya dehi me vacanasiddhividhānaṃ pārvatīpate hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hreṃ hrauṃ hraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ namo bhagavate rudrāya dehi me vacanasiddhividhānaṃ pārvatīpate hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hreṃ hrauṃ hraḥ</s>.

children.text: rātrau rātrau japen mantraṃ sāgarasya taṭe śuciḥ /
children.translated_text: One should recite the <s>mantra</s> at night, at night, on the seashore, being pure;

children.text: lakṣajāpe kṛte siddho datte sāgaraceṭakaḥ // UT_10.6
