children.translated_text: when a <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) recitations are completed, the ocean <s>ceṭaka</s> (servant-spirit) is accomplished. // UT 10.6

children.text: ratnatrayaṃ tadā maunyaṃ yasmin mantrī sukhī bhavet /
children.translated_text: Then [one obtains] three gems; at that time [one should observe] silence, by which the <s>mantrī</s> becomes happy.

children.text: sahasradaśakaṃ nityaṃ rātrau mantraṃ japet sudhīḥ // UT_10.7
children.translated_text: The wise one should recite the <s>mantra</s> ten thousand times daily at night. // UT 10.7

children.text: taddaśāṃśaṃ madhupayomiśraiḥ padmaiś ca homayet /
children.translated_text: One should offer a tenth of that as oblation with honey, milk, and lotuses.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate rudra dehi me nijarāśiṃ śrīṃ namo 'stu te svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ namo bhagavate rudra dehi me nijarāśiṃ śrīṃ namo 'stu te svāhā</s>.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ amukaṃ rañjaya svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ</s> [name] <s>rañjaya svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa sarvajanās tasmāt tu rañjakā bhavanti niśācaraṃ dhyātvā ātmapāṇinā japanād adṛśyakāriṇīṃ vidyām āpnoti // UT_10.8
children.translated_text: By this <s>mantra</s>, all people become enamored of him; meditating on the night-wanderer, by reciting with one's own hand, one obtains the <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) that makes one invisible. // UT 10.8

children.text: oṃ namo rasācāriṇe maheśvarāya mama paryaṭane sarvalokalocanāni bandhaya 2 devy ājñāpayati svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ namo rasācāriṇe maheśvarāya mama paryaṭane sarvalokalocanāni bandhaya bandhaya devy ājñāpayati svāhā</s>.

children.text: sakṛd uccāramātreṇa nṛsiṃhaceṭakākhyo mantro ḍākinyādidoṣaṃ nāśayati /
children.translated_text: By a single utterance, the <s>mantra</s> called <s>Nṛsiṃha-ceṭaka</s> destroys the affliction of <s>ḍākinīs</s> and the like.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate hiraṇyakaśipubalavidāraṇāya tribhuvanavyāpakāya bhūtapretapiśācakūṣmāṇḍabrahmarākṣasayoginīḍākinīkulonmūlanāya stambhodbhavāya samastadoṣān nāśaya 2 visara 2 kampaya 2 matha 2 hūṃ hṛṃ svāhā ehy ehi rudra ājñāpayati svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ namo bhagavate hiraṇyakaśipubalavidāraṇāya tribhuvanavyāpakāya bhūtapretapiśācakūṣmāṇḍabrahmarākṣasayoginīḍākinīkulonmūlanāya stambhodbhavāya samastadoṣān nāśaya nāśaya visara visara kampaya kampaya matha matha hūṃ hṛṃ svāhā ehy ehi rudra ājñāpayati svāhā</s>.

children.text: prerakaḥ sahasrapādaḥ anidrām ākarṣayati /
children.translated_text: <s>Preraka Sahasrapāda</s> (the Thousand-footed Impeller) attracts sleeplessness [upon the target].

children.text: oṃ preraka amukīṃ tava maṇḍalaṃ samāvartaya drāvaya dāhaya saṃtāpaya hauṃ // UT_10.9
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ preraka</s> [name] <s>tava maṇḍalaṃ samāvartaya drāvaya dāhaya saṃtāpaya hauṃ</s>. // UT 10.9

children.text: vajrakrodhāya mahādantāya daśadiśo bandha bandha haṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Vajrakrodhāya mahādantāya daśadiśo bandha bandha haṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: atha yonisaṃkocanam /
children.translated_text: Now <s>yoni-saṃkocana</s> (vaginal contraction):

children.text: kumudaṃ haritālaṃ ca piṣṭvā yoniṃ pralepayet /
children.translated_text: Having ground <s>kumuda</s> (white water-lily) and <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment), one should apply [them] to the <s>yoni</s>;

children.text: trirātraṃ pañcarātraṃ ca yonir bhavati saṃyutā // UT_11.1
children.translated_text: in three nights or five nights, the <s>yoni</s> becomes tightened. // UT 11.1

children.text: māṃsī candanamustā ca tagaraṃ nāgakesaram /
children.translated_text: <s>Māṃsī</s> (spikenard), sandalwood, <s>mustā</s> (nut grass), <s>tagara</s> (Indian valerian), and <s>nāgakesara</s> (Mesua ferrea)—

children.text: ebhir māsaprayogaṃ ca bhagalepanam uttamam // UT_11.2
children.translated_text: with these, a month's application is the supreme vaginal paste. // UT 11.2

children.text: mālatīkusumais tailair valkair varāṅgalepanam /
children.translated_text: With <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) flowers, oils, and barks—[this is] the body application for a beautiful woman;

children.text: ṛtukāle 'thavā kuryāt tadā tattulyatā bhavet // UT_11.3
children.translated_text: if done during the fertile period, then equality [in pleasure] is achieved. // UT 11.3

children.text: ḍimbasyānīya pañcāṅgaṃ sarṣapatailapācitam /
children.translated_text: Bringing the five parts of <s>ḍimba</s> (neem), cooked in mustard oil,

children.text: satatam abhilepena sā bhartāraṃ vaśaṃ nayet // UT_11.4
children.translated_text: by constant application, she brings her husband under control. // UT 11.4

children.text: mūlaṃ tu vānarīśṛṅgaṃ chāgīmūtreṇa lepayet /
children.translated_text: The root of <s>vānarīśṛṅga</s> (a plant)—one should apply [it] with she-goat's urine;

children.text: lepanāt tu tataḥ śiśnaṃ yathecchaṃ kāmayed balāt // UT_11.5
children.translated_text: from that application, the <s>śiśna</s> (penis) [becomes potent]—he can enjoy as desired with vigor. // UT 11.5

children.text: saubhāgyapippalī lākṣā viṣaṃ ca kramavardhitam /
children.translated_text: <s>Saubhāgya-pippalī</s> (auspicious long pepper), lac, and poison, progressively increased—

children.text: lepaṃ prakṣālitaṃ liṅgaṃ nārī kāmayate cirāt // UT_11.6
children.translated_text: when the anointed <s>liṅga</s> (penis) is washed, a woman desires [him] for a long time. // UT 11.6

children.text: pārāvataṃ tathā guñjā śvetotpalaṃ samakṣikam /
children.translated_text: Dove [parts], <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea), white lotus, with equal [portions of] honey—

children.text: nābhilepanam ity uktaṃ vīryastambhakaraṃ param // UT_11.7
children.translated_text: this is declared as a navel application, supreme for <s>vīryastambha</s> (semen retention). // UT 11.7

children.text: dvādaśāraṃ likhec cakraṃ kuṅkumena samanvitam /
children.translated_text: One should draw a twelve-spoked <s>cakra</s> (wheel/diagram) imbued with saffron

children.text: bhūrjapattre 'thavā vastre netre baddhaphalādike // UT_11.8
children.translated_text: on birch bark or cloth, with fruits and the like bound at the eyes. // UT 11.8

children.text: pattre pattre likhed bījaṃ hrīṃkāraṃ paramojjvalam /
children.translated_text: On each petal, one should write the seed-syllable <s>hrīṃ</s>, supremely radiant,

children.text: sādhyanāma tathā madhye karṇikāyāṃ viśeṣataḥ // UT_11.9
children.translated_text: and the name of the target in the center, especially in the pericarp. // UT 11.9

children.text: vidarbhamantramukhyena tatkūṭaṃ parimaṇḍale /
children.translated_text: With the chief <s>Vidarbha mantra</s>, its peak in the surrounding circle;

children.text: mṛttikābhiḥ samastābhiḥ pratimāṃ kārayed dṛḍham // UT_11.10
children.translated_text: one should make a firm image with all types of earth. // UT 11.10

children.text: karṣayet pramadāṃ nṝṇāṃ garvitāṃ tu na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: It attracts the proud women of men—there is no doubt;

children.text: vairāgyaṃ na punar yāti dāsībhāvena tiṣṭhati // UT_11.11
children.translated_text: aversion does not return—she remains in a state of servitude. // UT 11.11

children.text: dāḍimaṃ pañcakolaṃ ca lohaṃ vajrorasaṃ ghṛtam /
children.translated_text: Pomegranate, <s>pañcakola</s> (five spices), iron, <s>vajra</s>-mercury, and ghee;

children.text: cūrṇaṃ bhūmandarā śākhā dantanakhaṃ karoti vai // UT_11.12
children.translated_text: the powder of <s>bhūmandarā</s> branch makes nails and teeth [strong]. // UT 11.12

children.text: manaḥśilā prayaṅguś ca rocanā nāgakesaram /
children.translated_text: <s>Manaḥśilā</s> (realgar), <s>prayaṅgu</s> (panic grass), <s>gorocanā</s> (ox-bile pigment), and <s>nāgakesara</s>—

children.text: netrāñjanasamāyuktaṃ sarvasattvavaśaṃkaram // UT_11.13
children.translated_text: combined with eye-collyrium, [it] controls all beings. // UT 11.13

body.text:
Uḍḍāmareśvaratantra, Dvādaśaḥ paṭalaḥ
oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ draṃ caṇḍogre trinetre cāmuṇḍe ariṣṭe hūṃ phaṭ svāhā /

children.text: hrīṃ namāmy ahaṃ mahādevaṃ nṛsiṃhaṃ bhīmarūpiṇam oṃ namas tasmai /
children.translated_text: <s>Hrīṃ</s>—I bow to the great god <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, of terrifying form—<s>oṃ</s>, salutations to him.

children.text: śrīpārvaty uvāca /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Pārvatī</s> said:

children.text: uḍḍīśena samākīrṇe yogivṛndasamākule /
children.translated_text: In the assembly pervaded by <s>Uḍḍīśa</s>, crowded with groups of <s>yogins</s>,

children.text: praṇamya śirasā gaurī paripṛcchati śaṃkaram // UT_12.1
children.translated_text: bowing with her head, <s>Gaurī</s> asks <s>Śaṃkara</s>: // UT 12.1

children.text: śrīśvara uvāca /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Īśvara</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu tvaṃ hi varārohe siddhyarthaṃ prativāsase /
children.translated_text: Listen, O beautiful-hipped one, for the purpose of <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) you reside [here];

children.text: taṃ vadiṣyāmi te devi sarvaṃ tat samupāhṛtam // UT_12.2
children.translated_text: I shall tell you, O goddess, all that which has been gathered together. // UT 12.2

children.text: devi yo dvijo mantrais tu viprahanyān na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: O goddess, a twice-born [who knows these] <s>mantras</s> indeed destroys <s>vipras</s> (brahmins)—there is no doubt;

children.text: pūrvoditaṃ mayoḍḍīśaṃ kathyate tava bhaktitaḥ // UT_12.3
children.translated_text: the previously taught <s>Uḍḍīśa</s> [doctrine] is spoken to you out of devotion. // UT 12.3

children.text: uḍḍīśaṃ ca namaskṛtya rudraṃ caiva sudurjayam /
children.translated_text: Having saluted <s>Uḍḍīśa</s> and the unconquerable <s>Rudra</s>,

children.text: kapardinaṃ virūpākṣaṃ sarvabhūtabhayāvaham // UT_12.4
children.translated_text: the matted-haired one, the odd-eyed one, terrifying to all beings— // UT 12.4

children.text: prathamaṃ bhūtakaraṇaṃ dvitīyonmādanaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: first, the <s>bhūta</s>-ritual (spirit subjugation); second, causing madness;

children.text: tṛtīyaṃ dveṣaṇaṃ caiva turyam uccāṭanaṃ tathā // UT_12.5
children.translated_text: third, causing enmity; and fourth, causing expulsion. // UT 12.5

children.text: grāmoccāṭaṃ pañcamaṃ ca ṣaṣṭhaṃ ca jalastambhanam /
children.translated_text: Fifth, village expulsion; sixth, water-stilling;

children.text: saptamam agnistambhaṃ ca vaśīkaraṇam aṣṭamam // UT_12.6
children.translated_text: seventh, fire-stilling; and eighth, <s>vaśīkaraṇa</s> (subjugation). // UT 12.6

children.text: anyān api prayogāṃś ca śṛṇuṣva vai varānane /
children.translated_text: Hear also other practices, O beautiful-faced one;

children.text: śivena kathitā yogā uḍḍīśe śāstraniścaye // UT_12.7
children.translated_text: the <s>yogas</s> taught by <s>Śiva</s>, established in the <s>Uḍḍīśa śāstra</s>. // UT 12.7

children.text: andhī ca vandhīkaraṇaṃ mūkīkāras tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Making blind, making barren, making mute,

children.text: gātrasaṃkocanaṃ caiva bhūtajvarakaras tathā // UT_12.8
children.translated_text: body contraction, and causing <s>bhūta</s>-fever (spirit-possession fever). // UT 12.8

children.text: astraśastrasya truṭitaṃ pānīyasya vināśanam /
children.translated_text: Breaking of missiles and weapons, destruction of water,

children.text: dadhimadhunāśanaṃ ca nakhakaraṇaṃ tathaiva ca // UT_12.9
children.translated_text: destruction of curds and honey, and making nails [grow on the body]. // UT 12.9

children.text: gajānāṃ vājināṃ caiva prakopanaṃ parasparam /
children.translated_text: Agitating elephants and horses against each other,

children.text: ākarṣaṇaṃ bhujaṃgānāṃ mānavānāṃ tathā dhruvam // UT_12.10
children.translated_text: attracting serpents, and certainly [attracting] humans. // UT 12.10

children.text: sasyavināśanaṃ caiva garbhasyāntardhikāraṇam /
children.translated_text: Destruction of crops, and concealing the embryo,

children.text: vetālāñjanasiddhiś ca ulūkasiddhir api hi // UT_12.11
children.translated_text: <s>vetāla</s>-collyrium accomplishment, and owl accomplishment as well. // UT 12.11

children.text: anyān api mahāraudrān prayogān śṛṇu sāmpratam /
children.translated_text: Hear now also other most terrible practices—

children.text: vidyāmantraprayogāṃś ca auṣadhaṃ cābhicārikam // UT_12.12
children.translated_text: <s>vidyā</s>-<s>mantra</s> practices, and <s>abhicāra</s> (sorcery) medicines. // UT 12.12

children.text: guptā guptatarāḥ kāryā rakṣitavyāḥ prayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: They should be kept secret, most secret, and protected with great effort—

children.text: akulīnādhamabuddher bhaktihīnasya vai tathā // UT_12.13
children.translated_text: [hidden] from the uncultured, the base-minded, and the one devoid of devotion, // UT 12.13

children.text: hiṃsakasya ca kṣudrasya nindakasya viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: from the violent, the petty, and especially from the slanderer.

children.text: svārthaṃ phalādilubdhasya upadeśam amanyataḥ // UT_12.14
children.translated_text: for one's own benefit, of one greedy for fruits and such, who disregards the teaching— // UT 12.14

children.text: asmin śāpe pūruṣās te varjanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: In this curse, those persons should be carefully avoided;

children.text: etaiś ca saha saṃyogo na kāryaḥ sarvadā budhaiḥ // UT_12.15
children.translated_text: and association with them should never be made by the wise. // UT 12.15

children.text: ya uḍḍīśakriyāśaktibhedaṃ kurvanti mohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who, deluded, create divisions in the power of <s>Uḍḍīśa</s>'s practices—

children.text: te duṣṭā durjayāś caiva kim atra bahubhāṣitaiḥ // UT_12.16
children.translated_text: they are wicked and unconquerable—what need of many words? // UT 12.16

children.text: yadīcchāsiddhim ātmānam ātmārthaṃ hi tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: If one desires the attainment of one's self, for one's own purpose as well,

children.text: satpūruṣāya dātavyaṃ devagururatāya ca // UT_12.17
children.translated_text: it should be given to a virtuous person, one devoted to the <s>guru</s> and the gods. // UT 12.17

children.text: prayogās tu prayoktavyāḥ sādhakaiḥ śatrukāraṇe /
children.translated_text: Practices should be employed by <s>sādhakas</s> (practitioners) for the purpose of [subduing] enemies;

children.text: animittā nivartante svātmagrāhe na saṃśayaḥ // UT_12.18
children.translated_text: without cause they turn back upon oneself—there is no doubt. // UT 12.18

children.text: asaṃtuṣṭo hy ayuktaś ca prayogān iti nācaret /
children.translated_text: One who is discontented and undisciplined should not perform such practices;

children.text: śāstrasiddhavicārās tu sāmantakoṣakāḥ śubhāḥ // UT_12.19
children.translated_text: the deliberations established in the <s>śāstra</s> (scriptures) are auspicious, like neighboring treasuries. // UT 12.19

children.text: oṃ glauṃ gaṃ gaṇeśāya namaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ glauṃ gaṃ Gaṇeśāya namaḥ</s>.

children.text: mantreṇānena mantrajñaḥ kumbhakāramṛdā tathā /
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, the knower of <s>mantras</s>, using potter's clay,

children.text: lambodaraṃ prakurvīta pūjayed upacārakaiḥ // UT_12.20
children.translated_text: should fashion <s>Lambodara</s> (pot-bellied Gaṇeśa) and worship him with ritual offerings. // UT 12.20

children.text: sāptāhikaṃ trisaṃdhyāyāṃ japtavyaṃ sāvadhānataḥ /
children.translated_text: For seven days, at the three <s>sandhyās</s> (juncture-prayers), one should recite attentively,

children.text: sahasraikapramāṇena japāc chāntir bhaviṣyati // UT_12.21
children.translated_text: by reciting one thousand times, peace shall arise. // UT 12.21

children.text: prātar aṣṭottaraṃ japtvā labhed buddhiṃ śubhāṃ naraḥ /
children.translated_text: Having recited one hundred and eight times in the morning, a man obtains auspicious wisdom;

children.text: māsenaikena deveśi śrīlābhaś ca bhaved dhruvam // UT_12.22
children.translated_text: in one month, O Queen of Gods, the gain of <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) shall certainly occur. // UT 12.22

children.text: ṣaṇmāsena varārohe mahādhanapatir bhavet /
children.translated_text: In six months, O beautiful-hipped one, he becomes a great lord of wealth;

children.text: trikālajñānavettā ca varṣaikena na saṃśayaḥ // UT_12.23
children.translated_text: and a knower of the three times (past, present, future) in one year—there is no doubt. // UT 12.23

children.text: aiṃ namaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Aiṃ namaḥ svāhā</s>.

children.text: prātaḥ sahasravāraṃ tu prajaptena prapūjayet /
children.translated_text: In the morning, having recited a thousand times, one should worship

children.text: varadāṃ tu mahādevīṃ śvetagandhānulepanaiḥ // UT_12.24
children.translated_text: the boon-granting <s>Mahādevī</s> (great goddess) with white sandalwood paste. // UT 12.24

children.text: puṣpair jāpair dakṣiṇādisopacārais tu pratyaham /
children.translated_text: With flowers, recitations, <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (offerings) and other daily worship items—

children.text: saptame divase hy evaṃ vāgaiśvaryaṃ prajāyate // UT_12.25
children.translated_text: on the seventh day, thus, mastery of speech arises. // UT 12.25

children.text: bhavet sadyaḥ pravaktā ca śrutismṛtidharo 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: One immediately becomes an eloquent speaker, and a retainer of <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>;

children.text: bāndhavaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ cirāyuḥ sukham edhate // UT_12.26
children.translated_text: a friend of all beings, long-lived, he prospers in happiness. // UT 12.26

children.text: oṃ klīṃ mantreṇānena deveśi sādhakaḥ japam ārabhet /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ klīṃ</s>—with this <s>mantra</s>, O Queen of Gods, the <s>sādhaka</s> should commence recitation,

children.text: raktavastrāvṛto nityaṃ tathā kuṅkumajāṅgale // UT_12.27
children.translated_text: always clad in red garments and upon saffron-colored ground. // UT 12.27

children.text: saptāhajapamātreṇa hy ānayet tridaśāṅganām /
children.translated_text: By merely seven days of recitation, one attracts a celestial woman.

children.text: oṃ drīṃ drīṃ drīṃ drīṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ drīṃ drīṃ drīṃ drīṃ svāhā</s>.

children.text: pūrvavidhāno hi japed ekāntasaṃsthitaḥ // UT_12.28
children.translated_text: Following the previous method, one should recite while seated in solitude. // UT 12.28

children.text: ākarṣeti striyaṃ śastāṃ sālaṃkārāṃ suvāsasam /
children.translated_text: One attracts a praiseworthy woman, adorned with ornaments and fine garments.

children.text: oṃ haiṃ haḥ huṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ haiṃ haḥ huṃ</s>.

children.text: ūrdhvadṛṣṭiprayogeṇa japel lakṣatrayaṃ priye // UT_12.29
children.translated_text: With the practice of upward gaze, one should recite three <s>lakṣas</s> (three hundred thousand times), O beloved. // UT 12.29

children.text: sarvapāpavinirmukto jāyate khecare pade /
children.translated_text: Freed from all sins, one is born in the state of a <s>khecara</s> (sky-traveler).

children.text: oṃ drīṃ kārīṇḍaḥ kṣaḥ kṣīṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ drīṃ kārīṇḍaḥ kṣaḥ kṣīṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: ekapādasthito bhadre japed aṣṭottaraṃ śatam // UT_12.30
children.translated_text: Standing on one foot, O auspicious one, one should recite one hundred and eight times. // UT 12.30

children.text: yad yat prārthayate vastu tad dadāti dine dine /
children.translated_text: Whatever object one desires, it is granted day after day;

children.text: yajen naraviśeṣaṃ ca devāgnigurubrāhmaṇaiḥ // UT_12.31
children.translated_text: one should worship distinguished men together with gods, fire, the <s>guru</s>, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. // UT 12.31

children.text: oṃ śrīṃ kṣīṃ lohaṃ muñca kili kili amukaṃ kāṭaya kāṭaya mātaṃgini svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ śrīṃ kṣīṃ lohaṃ muñca kili kili</s> [name] <s>kāṭaya kāṭaya mātaṃgini svāhā</s>.

children.text: mantreṇānena pūrvāhṇe pūjayann upacārakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, in the forenoon, worshipping with ritual offerings,

children.text: śarāvaṃ pūrayitvā tu catuṣpathe baliṃ haret // UT_12.32
children.translated_text: having filled a bowl, one should carry the <s>bali</s> (offering) to a crossroads. // UT 12.32

children.text: samantraṃ kṣipyati pumān puruṣaṃ yadi paśyati /
children.translated_text: If a man throws [it] with the <s>mantra</s> and sees a person,

children.text: ātmacintitakāryāṇi sādhayaty eva nānyathā // UT_12.33
children.translated_text: the tasks conceived in his mind are accomplished, not otherwise. // UT 12.33

children.text: oṃ stambhini svāhā kapālini svāhā drīṃ drīṃ vaiṣādārthini svāhā chaḥ chaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ stambhini svāhā kapālini svāhā drīṃ drīṃ vaiṣādārthini svāhā chaḥ chaḥ</s>.

children.text: mantreṇa mṛttikāṃ japtvā pratārya saptadhā jale /
children.translated_text: Having recited the <s>mantra</s> over clay, casting it seven times into water,

children.text: saṃmukhībhūya kṣiptvā ca japtvā cāyutaṃ vāsare // UT_12.34
children.translated_text: having thrown it face-to-face and recited ten thousand times in [a single] day— // UT 12.34

children.text: tena siddho bhaven mantraḥ sādhakasya na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: by that the <s>mantra</s> becomes accomplished for the practitioner, there is no doubt.

children.text: oṃ śrīṃ kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣaiṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ śrīṃ kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣaiṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ</s>.

children.text: madhyāhnasamaye sūryasammukhe japam ācaret // UT_12.35
children.translated_text: At midday, facing the sun, one should perform recitation. // UT 12.35

children.text: ayutaṃ japtamātreṇa svasāmarthyaṃ prapaśyati /
children.translated_text: By merely reciting ten thousand times, one perceives one's own power;

children.text: tasya dṛṣṭinipātena dvipadaś ca catuṣpadaḥ // UT_12.36
children.translated_text: by the fall of his gaze, both bipeds and quadrupeds— // UT 12.36

children.text: jvarābhibhūtā jāyante apūrvā mantrasampadaḥ /
children.translated_text: become afflicted by fever; such are the extraordinary powers of the <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: oṃ haṃsaḥ haṃsaṃ so 'haṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ haṃsaḥ haṃsaṃ so'haṃ svāhā</s>.

children.text: ekaviṃśatijaptena jalena jvarapīḍitaḥ // UT_12.37
children.translated_text: With water consecrated by twenty-one recitations, one afflicted by fever— // UT 12.37

children.text: vimucyate pānamātrāt sadyaḥ svasthaś ca jāyate /
children.translated_text: is freed merely by drinking it, and immediately becomes well.

children.text: oṃ drīṃ namo ghoreśvari ghoramukhi cāmuṇḍe ūrdhvakeśi vikṛtānane drīṃ drīṃ huṃ phaṭ huṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ drīṃ namo Ghoreśvari ghoramukhi Cāmuṇḍe ūrdhvakeśi vikṛtānane drīṃ drīṃ huṃ phaṭ huṃ svāhā</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ sarvadalanamantraḥ // UT_12.38
children.translated_text: This is the <s>mantra</s> for destroying everything. // UT 12.38

children.text:
oṃ drīṃ drīṃ drīṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā sarvagrahāṇāṃ trāsanaṃ kuru kuru aṅguliprahāreṇa /
oṃ sraṃ srāṃ sriṃ srīṃ sruṃ srūṃ sreṃ sraiṃ sroṃ srauṃ sraṃ sraḥ ha raṃ rauṃ rīṃ rūṃ raiṃ reviḥ chuṃ chuṃ haṃsaḥ amṛtavarcase svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ drīṃ drīṃ drīṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā</s>—cause terror among all <s>grahas</s> (seizing spirits), do it, do it, with a finger-strike! <s>Oṃ sraṃ srāṃ sriṃ srīṃ sruṃ srūṃ sreṃ sraiṃ sroṃ srauṃ sraṃ sraḥ ha raṃ rauṃ rīṃ rūṃ raiṃ reviḥ chuṃ chuṃ haṃsaḥ amṛtavarcase svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇodakaṃ śarāvaṃ saṃkṣipyāṣṭottaraśatenābhimantritaṃ kṛtvā pibet prātar utthāya saṃvatsareṇa vallīpalitavarjito bhavati /
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, having placed water in a bowl, consecrated one hundred and eight times, one should drink it upon waking in the morning; in one year, one becomes free of wrinkles and grey hair.

children.text: vṛkṣasthāvarajaṅgamākṛtiṃ samāṅgīkārāc ca vyāghralomādikaṃ pūrvodaryāṃ bhasmīkaroti sarvajanapriyo bhavati cirāyur bhavati /
children.translated_text: By assimilating the form of trees, stationary and moving beings, and by [using] tiger hair and such in the previous manner, one reduces [afflictions] to ashes; one becomes dear to all people and long-lived.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate rudrāya caṇḍeśvarāya huṃ huṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ namo bhagavate Rudrāya Caṇḍeśvarāya huṃ huṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa japaṃ kṛtvā śīghram īpsitaṃ labhet // UT_12.39
children.translated_text: By performing recitation with this <s>mantra</s>, one quickly obtains the desired [result]. // UT 12.39

children.text:
oṃ hūṃ drīṃ kṣaṃ kṣāṃ kṣiṃ kṣīṃ kṣuṃ kṣūṃ kṣeṃ kṣaiṃ kṣoṃ kṣauṃ kṣaṃ kṣaḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā /
imaṃ mantraṃ pūrvaṃ lakṣam ekaṃ japet taddaśāṃśam ayutaṃ havanaṃ kuryāt /
ekaikaṃ samidhaṃ ghṛtāktāṃ juhuyāt siddho bhavati gaṅgāgoloke na te meghāḥ praṇaśyanti na ca varṣanti vāsavo nadasamudraṃ śoṣayati meghastambho bhavati /
udakamadhye sthitvā japaṃ karoty anāvṛṣṭikāle 'tivṛṣṭiṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hūṃ drīṃ kṣaṃ kṣāṃ kṣiṃ kṣīṃ kṣuṃ kṣūṃ kṣeṃ kṣaiṃ kṣoṃ kṣauṃ kṣaṃ kṣaḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>. One should first recite this <s>mantra</s> one <s>lakṣa</s> (hundred thousand) times; then perform a <s>havana</s> (fire oblation) of one-tenth that, ten thousand times. One should offer each <s>samidh</s> (sacrificial stick) smeared with ghee; [then] one becomes accomplished. In the region of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the clouds do not disperse, nor does <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra) cause rain; one dries up rivers and oceans—a stoppage of clouds occurs. Standing in the midst of water and performing recitation, during a time of drought, one causes torrential rain.

children.text: oṃ drīṃ pracalite kubere hūṃ hūṃ kili kili svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ drīṃ pracalite Kubere hūṃ hūṃ kili kili svāhā</s>.

children.text: pūrvavelāyām ādarśadīpasamīpe ṣaḍaṅgulena bhājane sūryamaṇḍale kumāraṃ vāme veśayati pūrvam ayutajapaḥ kartavyaḥ pañcopacāreṇa pūjā ca kartavyā pūrvābhiś ca svarājye /
children.translated_text: In the early morning, near a mirror and a lamp, in a vessel six finger-widths [wide], upon the solar disc, one should seat a boy to the left. First, ten thousand recitations should be performed, along with worship using the five offerings, and with the previous [mantras] for sovereignty.

children.text: oṃ śrīṃ himajāte prayaccha me dhanaṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ śrīṃ himajāte prayaccha me dhanaṃ svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa siddhārthakaṃ ghṛtamiśritaṃ hunet aṣṭottaraśate na annapānavimiśritaṃ sahasreṇa hunet manasaḥ prārthitaṃ labhet ayutaṃ hunec chrīsumanā bhavet lakṣaṃ huned grāmaśataṃ labhet // UT_12.40
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, one should offer <s>siddhārthaka</s> (white mustard) mixed with ghee: with one hundred and eight [oblations], mixed with food and drink; with a thousand oblations, one obtains what the mind desires; with ten thousand oblations, one becomes auspiciously prosperous; with one <s>lakṣa</s> oblations, one obtains a hundred villages. // UT 12.40

children.text: oṃ namo namaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ namo namaḥ</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ śataṃ japet sarvakāmaprado 'yaṃ mantraḥ // UT_12.41
children.translated_text: One should recite this <s>mantra</s> a hundred times; this <s>mantra</s> fulfills all desires. // UT 12.41

children.text: oṃ drīṃ śrīṃ sārase siddhikari krīṃ namaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ drīṃ śrīṃ sārase siddhikari krīṃ namaḥ svāhā</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ lakṣam ekaṃ japed raktakaravīraiś ca pūjayet satataṃ sarvakāmado 'yaṃ mantraḥ // UT_12.42
children.translated_text: One should recite this <s>mantra</s> one <s>lakṣa</s> times and worship constantly with red oleander flowers; this <s>mantra</s> fulfills all desires. // UT 12.42

children.text: oṃ druṃ kṣeṃ kṣeṃ huṃ kṣaḥ amukaṃ kṣaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ druṃ kṣeṃ kṣeṃ huṃ kṣaḥ</s> [name] <s>kṣaḥ svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa rājikālavaṇatuṣakaṇṭakaśivanirmālyaṃ tailena yutaṃ hunet samastaśrībhājanaṃ bhavati // UT_12.43
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, one should offer mustard seeds, salt, husks, thorns, and <s>Śiva</s>'s <s>nirmālya</s> (discarded worship offerings) mixed with oil; one becomes a vessel of complete prosperity. // UT 12.43

children.text: oṃ huṃ huṃ huṃ lūṃ laṃ lauṃ huṃ laḥ amukaṃ chaḥ chaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ huṃ huṃ huṃ lūṃ laṃ lauṃ huṃ laḥ</s> [name] <s>chaḥ chaḥ svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa siddhārthaṃ bhasmanā saha mantritaṃ kartavyaṃ yasya gṛhe prakṣipya mantrabalipāṃśvair ākṣipet tasya bāhustambho bhavati /
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, one should consecrate <s>siddhārtha</s> (white mustard) together with ashes; when thrown into someone's house with the consecrated <s>bali</s> (offering) powders, paralysis of the arms occurs for that person.

children.text: ripusainyāgre kṣipet śatrusainyastambho bhavati aśvagajanarā niśceṣṭā bhavanti vikalā bhavanti samantādevākulā bhavanti // UT_12.44
children.translated_text: When thrown before an enemy's army, the enemy army is paralyzed; horses, elephants, and men become motionless, become disabled, and become agitated all around. // UT 12.44

children.text:
oṃ ruṃ ruṃ mukhe svāhā /
anena mantreṇa japtatailena mukhaṃ prakṣālya tilatailena gātrābhyaṅgaṃ vā vidhāya vātādikaṃ dinasaptakena naśyati /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ ruṃ ruṃ mukhe svāhā</s>. With this <s>mantra</s>, washing the face with consecrated oil, or anointing the body with sesame oil, ailments caused by <s>vāta</s> (wind) and so forth are destroyed within seven days.

children.text: aiṃ mātaṃgi vimalāvati vikarāle drīṃ chaḥ chaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Aiṃ Mātaṃgi Vimalāvati vikārāle drīṃ chaḥ chaḥ svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa japāpuṣpaṃ parijapya vārīṇi nadyādau homayet saptāhena īpsitaṃ phalaṃ labhet /
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, having consecrated <s>japā</s> (hibiscus) flowers and water, one should offer oblations at a river or such; in seven days one obtains the desired fruit.

children.text: kārtavīryārjuno nāma rājā bāhusahasrabhṛt /
children.translated_text: <s>Kārtavīryārjuna</s> by name, the king who bore a thousand arms—

children.text: tannāmakīrtanād eva hṛtaṃ naṣṭaṃ ca labhyate // UT_12.45
children.translated_text: by merely reciting his name, what was stolen or lost is recovered. // UT 12.45

children.text:
nityaṃ nityaṃ japet kiṃcid vidyāṃ vittasya prāptaye /
oṃ maṃ kiṇi svāhā /
iti vṛścikamantraḥ /
oṃ huṃ huṃ haṃsaḥ haṃsaṃ so 'haṃ so 'haṃ svāhā /
iti sarvaviṣāpaharaṇamantraḥ /
mayūrapicchena kuśena śareṇa śaradaṇḍena vā taddehe sammārjanaṃ kuryāt /
children.translated_text: One should always recite some <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge) for the attainment of wealth. <s>Oṃ maṃ kiṇi svāhā</s>—this is the scorpion <s>mantra</s>. <s>Oṃ huṃ huṃ haṃsaḥ haṃsaṃ so'haṃ so'haṃ svāhā</s>—this is the <s>mantra</s> for removing all poisons. One should sweep the body [of the afflicted] with a peacock feather, <s>kuśa</s> grass, an arrow, or a reed stalk.

children.text: haṃ hāṃ hiṃ hīṃ huṃ hūṃ heṃ haiṃ hoṃ hauṃ haṃ haḥ chaḥ chaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Haṃ hāṃ hiṃ hīṃ huṃ hūṃ heṃ haiṃ hoṃ hauṃ haṃ haḥ chaḥ chaḥ svāhā</s>.

children.text: imaṃ gokṣīrasadṛśaṃ vāraṃ vāraṃ vicintayed vā varānanamukhe śirasi śarīre tataḥ kaṇṭhe tato hṛdi nābhimaṇḍale guhye tathā sarvāṅge cintayet tathā pūrakeṇa varārohe kaṇṭhadaṣṭo 'pi jīvati /
children.translated_text: One should visualize this [mantra] as resembling cow's milk, again and again, on the face of the auspicious one, then on the head, then on the body, then on the throat, then on the heart, at the navel circle, at the private parts, and likewise over the entire body. With <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation), O beautiful-hipped one, even one bitten on the throat survives.

children.text: oṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye mahāgaṇapataye vighnaharāya mataṃgasambhavāya lambodarāya gaurīpriyaputrāya hrīṃ gāṃ namaḥ raṃ haṃ kṣaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ gaṃ Gaṇapataye mahāgaṇapataye vighnaharāya mataṃgasambhavāya lambodarāya Gaurīpriyaputrāya hrīṃ gāṃ namaḥ raṃ haṃ kṣaḥ svāhā</s>.

children.text: gorocanāviṣarājikāpippalīnīcayavair mahātailena saha devadattaiś ca lakṣitān ālikhet nimbakāṣṭhena pratikṛtiṃ hutvā pṛṣṭhato likhet sadyo jvaravilopo bhavati śāntir bhavati // UT_12.46
children.translated_text: One should write with a neem-wood [stylus] a figure [inscribed] with <s>gorocanā</s> (ox bile pigment), <s>viṣa</s> (poison), mustard, <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper), and <s>nīca</s> (castor) seeds, with great oil along with prescribed [substances], and offer it; writing on the back—immediately the fever is destroyed and peace ensues. // UT 12.46

body.translated_text:
<s>Uḍḍāmareśvaratantra</s>, Twelfth Chapter.
<s>Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ draṃ caṇḍogre trinetre cāmuṇḍe ariṣṭe hūṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

body.text:
Uḍḍāmareśvaratantra, Trayodaśaḥ paṭalaḥ
oṃ drīṃ vidyāstambhini stambhini chaḥ chaḥ svāhā /
imaṃ mantraṃ prathamam ayutam ekaṃ japet paścān manasā saṃsmaret /
vanamadhye 'pi bhojanaṃ prāpnoti /
oṃ hauṃ namo bhagavate mahārudrāya uḍḍāmareśvarāya huṃ huṃ chaṃ chaṃ drīṃ drīṃ svāhā /
anena mantreṇābhiṣekārthaṃ sahasravārajaptaṃ kalaśaṃ kārayet tanmadhye pañcaratnaṃ nidhāya śvetavastreṇa veṣṭayet nānāphalasusaṃcūrṇaṃ nānāratnopaśobhitaṃ taddvārakagṛhavāsaṃ kalaśaṃ dhṛtvā rātrau striyā saha śmaśāne vanaspatau vā ekavṛkṣe vā sarittaṭe samudragāminyāṃ nadyāṃ vā catuṣpathe vā gacchet /
tataś ca kalaśaṃ nītvā strī vandhyā vā mṛtavatsā vā durbhagā vā kākavandhyā vā bhaṅgā sarvajanapriyā bhavati pīḍitā udvartayet /

children.text: priyaṅguḥ kuṅkumaṃ gorocanā nāgakesaro dūrvā haridre dve siddhārthakadvayaṃ vacā punarnavāpāmārgo 'rkaś citrakaṃ śālmalī lakṣmaṇā tālamūlī śatāvarī vandhyā karkaṭī balā kṣīriṇī mṛgapippalī tathā cirāṇi supattrāṇy uśīraṃ ghṛtaṃ madhu tathā palāśapuṣpapattrāṇi ambarabilvapattrāṇy aśvagandhādīni sugandhadravyāṇi sarvāṇi sarve sādhyaviśeṣataḥ anyad udvartayed gātraṃ śirolepano yaḥ punaḥ kalaśaṃ prakṣipya snāpayet labhate striyaṃ sadā udvartanavastraṃ tyaktvā paravastraparidhānaṃ kuryāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṅgu</s> (beauty-berry), saffron, <s>gorocanā</s> (ox bile pigment), <s>nāgakesara</s> (Mesua), <s>dūrvā</s> (Bermuda grass), the two <s>haridrās</s> (turmeric and tree turmeric), two kinds of <s>siddhārthaka</s> (white mustard), <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag), <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia), <s>apāmārga</s> (prickly chaff flower), <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), <s>citraka</s> (leadwort), <s>śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton tree), <s>lakṣmaṇā</s> (a plant), <s>tālamūlī</s> (a plant), <s>śatāvarī</s> (Asparagus), <s>vandhyā karkaṭī</s> (barren cucumber), <s>balā</s> (Sida cordifolia), <s>kṣīriṇī</s> (a milky plant), <s>mṛgapippalī</s> (wild long pepper), also rags, fragrant leaves, <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver), ghee, honey, also <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) flower-leaves, <s>ambara</s> cloth and <s>bilva</s> (wood apple) leaves, <s>aśvagandhā</s> and other fragrant substances—all [should be prepared] according to the specific purpose. One should massage the body with another [preparation]; the head-paste [is applied] again. Having placed [all] into the <s>kalaśa</s>, one should bathe [the person]; the woman thus obtains [her desire]. Having discarded the massage-cloth, one should wear another's garment.

children.text: bhadrāsane vyavasthitā [... au4 Zeichenjh] kuryād vāri niḥkṣipya kumbhasthitaṃ yā strīṇāṃ madhye samākarṣayati yantraṃ tatas tāṃ sammukhastriyam arcayet /
children.translated_text: Seated on a <s>bhadrāsana</s> (auspicious seat) [...text damaged...], having placed water from the pot-dwelling [vessel], she who attracts among women—then one should worship that woman facing one,

children.text: vastrālaṃkārasindūrasugandhikusumādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: with garments, ornaments, <s>sindūra</s> (vermillion), fragrances, flowers, and such.

children.text: gṛhārcāṃ kārayed devaṃ śivaṃ devyā sahārcayet // UT_13.1
children.translated_text: One should establish <s>Śiva</s> for home worship, and worship him together with the <s>Devī</s> (Goddess). // UT 13.1

children.text: dakṣiṇāṃ sa pumān dadyāt śvetāṃ gāṃ vatsasaṃyutām /
children.translated_text: That man should give as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (offering) a white cow accompanied by her calf.

children.text: atha snānaphalaṃ vakṣye yathoktaṃ tripurāriṇā // UT_13.2
children.translated_text: Now I shall describe the fruit of the bathing, as spoken by <s>Tripurāri</s> (Śiva, destroyer of the three cities). // UT 13.2

children.text: putrārthī labhate putraṃ dhanārthī labhate dhanam /
children.translated_text: One desiring a son obtains a son; one desiring wealth obtains wealth;

children.text: śāntyarthī śāntim āpnoti durbhagā subhagā bhavet // UT_13.3
children.translated_text: one desiring peace attains peace; an unfortunate woman becomes fortunate. // UT 13.3

children.text: bhraṣṭarājyas tathā rājā rājyaṃ prāpnoti niścitam /
children.translated_text: And a king who has lost his kingdom surely regains his kingdom;

children.text: abhāryo labhate bhāryāṃ sukhārthī sukham āpnuyāt // UT_13.4
children.translated_text: one without a wife obtains a wife; one desiring happiness may attain happiness. // UT 13.4

children.text: iti strīpuruṣayoḥ snānaphalam // UT_13.5
children.translated_text: Thus is the fruit of bathing for both women and men. // UT 13.5

children.text: huṃ amukaṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Huṃ</s> [name] <s>huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: śmaśāne gatvā ulūkakapotakāñjīrāṇām atisatvaraṃ stanyaṃ gṛhītvā japet saptāhena // UT_13.6
children.translated_text: Having gone to a cremation ground, having quickly obtained the milk of owls, pigeons, and fig trees, one should recite for seven days. // UT 13.6

children.text: huṃ amukaṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā anena mantreṇa bhānuvṛkṣasamīpe sthitvāyutaikaṃ japet tataḥ kaṭutailena daśāṃśena havanaṃ kuryāt nipātīkaraṇaṃ bhavati // UT_13.7
children.translated_text: <s>Huṃ</s> [name] <s>phaṭ phaṭ svāhā</s>—with this <s>mantra</s>, standing near a <s>bhānu</s> (sun) tree, one should recite ten thousand times; then perform a <s>havana</s> (fire oblation) of one-tenth with pungent oil; it causes downfall. // UT 13.7

children.text: oṃ oṃ oṃ iti mantraṃ pūrvam ayutaṃ japtvānāvṛṣṭikāle japen mahāvṛṣṭir bhavati /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ oṃ oṃ</s>—having first recited this <s>mantra</s> ten thousand times, when one recites during a time of drought, great rainfall occurs.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ varade svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ varade svāhā</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ pūrvam ayutaṃ japtvā taddaśāṃśaṃ palāśasamidbhir havanaṃ kuryāt ghṛtaṃ hunet tataḥ sārvakālikaṃ phalaṃ labhet /
children.translated_text: Having first recited this <s>mantra</s> ten thousand times, one should perform a <s>havana</s> with <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) sacrificial sticks for one-tenth of that, offering ghee; then one obtains the fruit for all times.

children.text: huṃ huṃ huṃ naṃ naṃ naṃ amukaṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Huṃ huṃ huṃ naṃ naṃ naṃ</s> [name] <s>huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ pūrvam ayutaṃ japtvā khādirasamidho rudhireṇa liptvā taddaśāṃśaṃ hunet yasya nāmnā sa sahasraikena mahendrajvareṇa gṛhyate ayutahavanena nipātanaṃ tathānenaiva mantreṇāpāmārgasamidho hunet ayutasaṃkhyakāḥ trimadhuyutāḥ tato vibhīṣaṇādayo rākṣasā varadā bhavanti // UT_13.8
children.translated_text: Having first recited this <s>mantra</s> ten thousand times, smearing <s>khadira</s> (Acacia) sacrificial sticks with blood, one should offer one-tenth of that; whosoever's name [is used], that person is seized by the great fever of <s>Mahendra</s> with one thousand [oblations]; with ten thousand oblations, there is downfall. Likewise, with this very <s>mantra</s>, one should offer <s>apāmārga</s> (prickly chaff flower) sacrificial sticks, ten thousand in number, mixed with the three sweet substances; then <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> and other <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons) become boon-granters. // UT 13.8

children.text: oṃ hūṃ vāṃ vīṃ vūṃ vaiṃ vauṃ vaṃ vaḥ oṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hūṃ vāṃ vīṃ vūṃ vaiṃ vauṃ vaṃ vaḥ oṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ jvaragrahaṇamantraḥ // UT_13.9
children.translated_text: This is the <s>mantra</s> for seizing fever. // UT 13.9

children.text: oṃ aiṃ kṣili kili phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ aiṃ kṣili kili phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa trimadhuyuktam uḍumbaraṃ pūrvam ayutaṃ japtvā sahasraikaṃ homayed anāvṛṣṭikāle mahāvṛṣṭiṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, having first recited ten thousand times, one should offer one thousand oblations of <s>uḍumbara</s> (fig wood) mixed with the three sweets—during a time of drought, it produces great rain.

children.text: oṃ drāṃ drīṃ drūṃ draiṃ drauṃ haḥ oṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ drāṃ drīṃ drūṃ draiṃ drauṃ haḥ oṃ svāhā</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ pūrvam ayutaṃ japtvā trimadhuyutā bilvasamidho hunet tataḥ samastajanapadāḥ kiṃkarā bhavanti // UT_13.10
children.translated_text: Having first recited this <s>mantra</s> ten thousand times, one should offer oblations of <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) sticks mixed with the three sweets—then all the people of the realm become servants. // UT 13.10

children.text: oṃ drīṃ oṃ drīṃ huṃ oṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ drīṃ oṃ drīṃ huṃ oṃ svāhā</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ pūrvam ayutaṃ japtvā taddaśāṃśaṃ darbhasamidho ghṛtakṣīrayutā huned ayutahomataḥ sarvarogapraśāntir bhavati /
children.translated_text: Having first recited this <s>mantra</s> ten thousand times, one should offer oblations of one-tenth that amount of <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass) sticks mixed with ghee and milk—by ten thousand oblations, the pacification of all diseases occurs.

children.text: oṃ klīṃ amukīṃ khe khe svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ klīṃ amukīṃ khe khe svāhā</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ pūrvam ayutaṃ tu juhuyāt taddaśāṃśaṃ nyagrodhasamidho madhuyuktā hunet sahasramātrahomena mahārājapatnī vaśagā bhavati anyalokastrīṇāṃ tu kā kathā // UT_13.11
children.translated_text: Having first recited this <s>mantra</s> ten thousand times, one should offer one-tenth that amount of <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) sticks mixed with honey—by a mere thousand oblations, a great king's wife comes under one's control; what then to speak of women of other [lower] stations? // UT 13.11

children.text: oṃ drīṃ gomukhi gomukhi sahasrasutālā bhīmabhogapiśitabhūmau āgacchatu svāhā // UT_13.12
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ drīṃ gomukhi gomukhi sahasrasutālā bhīmabhogapiśitabhūmau āgacchatu svāhā</s>. // UT 13.12

children.text: anena mantreṇa raktakaravīraṃ kṣaudreṇa saṃyuktaṃ hunet vaśakāmo lavaṇaṃ hunet striyam ākarṣayati pūrvasaṃyuktaṃ premakāmaḥ sindūraṃ hunet purakṣobho bhavati tuṣakaraṭaṃ huned abhicārakarma bhavati mahāmāṃsaṃ ghṛtasaṃyuktaṃ hunet mahādhanapatir bhavet // UT_13.13
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>: one who desires subjugation should offer red <s>karavīra</s> (oleander) mixed with honey; one should offer salt—it attracts a woman; one desiring love should offer <s>sindūra</s> (vermillion) mixed with the aforesaid—it causes agitation in a city; one should offer husk and chaff—it becomes a rite of <s>abhicāra</s> (black magic); one should offer great flesh mixed with ghee—one becomes a lord of great wealth. // UT 13.13

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate rudrāya uḍḍāmareśvarāya huṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ namo bhagavate Rudrāya Uḍḍāmareśvarāya huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa śrīphalasaṃyuktaṃ ghṛtaṃ hunet śatahomena prajñā bhavati sahasreṇa golābho bhavati lakṣeṇa grāmasahasralābho bhavati sapādalakṣeṇa bhraṣṭarājyaṃ rājā prāpnoti // UT_13.14
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, one should offer ghee mixed with <s>śrīphala</s> (bilva fruit)—by a hundred oblations, wisdom arises; by a thousand, one obtains cattle; by a hundred thousand, one obtains a thousand villages; by one hundred and twenty-five thousand, a king who has lost his kingdom regains it. // UT 13.14

children.text: oṃ aiṃ drīṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ aiṃ drīṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa kākamāṃsaṃ kukkuṭabījaṃ kaṭutailena hunet sahasraikena drīṃkārāntaṃ nāma saṃjapya yasya nāmnā japet sa conmatto bhavati sahasraikena taṇḍulahomena sustho bhavati // UT_13.15
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, one should offer crow's flesh and hen's egg with pungent oil—having recited a thousand and one times, ending with "<s>drīṃ</s>," whispering the name of the target, that person becomes maddened; by a thousand and one oblations of rice grains, the person is restored to health. // UT 13.15

children.text:
oṃ aiṃ śrīṃ kṣaṃ klīṃ svāhā /
anena mantreṇa japaḥ kāryaḥ saptavārajaptena dehaśuddhir bhavati śatajaptena sarvatīrthasnānaphalaṃ bhavati sahasreṇa dhīvṛddhiḥ ayutena sahasragranthakartā mahān kavir bhavati ekalakṣeṇa śrutidharo bhavati dvilakṣeṇa samastaśāstrajño bhavati trilakṣeṇātītānāgatavartamānajño bhavati caturlakṣeṇa grahapatir bhavati pañcalakṣeṇa vedavedāntapurāṇasmṛtiviśeṣajño bhavati ṣaḍlakṣair vajratantur bhavati saptalakṣair nadīṃ śoṣayati hariharabrahmādiṣu sakhyaṃ bhavati nocet vajroktena vidhinā japet tadā saṃskṛto 'yaṃ darśakena vā maharṣiṇā śatena samo bhavati sahasreṇa saṃtāparahito bhavati punar apy ayutena purakṣobhako bhavati ṣaḍguṇena trailokyaṃ kṣobhayati tṛtīyena saptapātālaṃ kṣobhayati caturthena svargaṃ kṣobhayati pañcamenordhvagān saptalokān kṣobhayati ṣaḍguṇena trailokyaṃ kṣobhayati saptamena dvipadacatuṣpadādiprāṇimātraṃ kṣobhayati aṣṭamena sthāvarajaṅgamam ākarṣayati navamena svayam eva sarvalokeṣu nāradavad anāvṛtagatir bhavati daśalakṣeṇa kartum akartum anyathā kartuṃ kṣamo bhavati /
punar apy amṛtakṣepaṇavidhinā japet sakṛd api naraḥ śvetakaravīrakusumatrimadhuyuktām āhutiṃ dadyāt sarvajanapriyo bhavati aśokapuṣpāṇi saghṛtaṃ hunet śokarahito bhavati bhraṣṭarājyaprāptikāmaḥ śrīphalahomaṃ kuryāt bhraṣṭarājyaṃ prāpnoti ājyayuktapadmapuṣpāṇi athavā kumudinīpuṣpāṇi homayet /
nipātakāmaḥ kaṭutailayuktaṃ mayūramāṃsaṃ hunet kūṭena maraṇaṃ bhavati /
pūgīphalaṃ kaṭutailaṃ lohacūrṇaṃ ca hunet samastadehe visphoṭakā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
<s>Oṃ aiṃ śrīṃ kṣaṃ klīṃ svāhā</s>.
With this <s>mantra</s>, <s>japa</s> (recitation) should be performed: by reciting seven times, purification of the body occurs; by a hundred recitations, the fruit of bathing in all sacred waters is obtained; by a thousand, increase of intellect; by ten thousand, one becomes a composer of a thousand treatises, a great poet; by one hundred thousand, one becomes a retainer of the <s>Vedas</s>; by two hundred thousand, one becomes a knower of all <s>śāstras</s> (sciences); by three hundred thousand, one becomes a knower of past, future, and present; by four hundred thousand, one becomes a lord of planets; by five hundred thousand, one becomes a special knower of <s>Vedas</s>, <s>Vedānta</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and <s>Smṛtis</s>; by six hundred thousand, one becomes [endowed with] a vajra thread; by seven hundred thousand, one dries up a river and attains friendship with <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and others. If not, one should recite according to the method stated in the <s>Vajra</s> [text]—then, being thus consecrated, by a seer or by a beholder, one becomes equal to a great sage by a hundred; by a thousand, one becomes free from affliction; again by ten thousand, one becomes an agitator of cities; by six times that, one agitates the three worlds; by the third [multiple], one agitates the seven netherworlds; by the fourth, one agitates heaven; by the fifth, one agitates the seven upper worlds; by six times, one agitates the three worlds; by the seventh, one agitates all beings with two feet, four feet, and so on; by the eighth, one attracts all that is stationary and moving; by the ninth, one oneself becomes, like <s>Nārada</s>, one with unobstructed movement in all worlds; by ten hundred thousand, one becomes capable of doing, undoing, and doing otherwise.
Furthermore, one should recite according to the method of <s>amṛtakṣepaṇa</s> (nectar-sprinkling): if a person offers even a single oblation of white oleander flowers mixed with the three sweets, he becomes beloved of all people; if one offers <s>aśoka</s> flowers with ghee, one becomes free from sorrow; one desiring to regain a lost kingdom should perform a <s>homa</s> of <s>śrīphala</s>—one regains the lost kingdom; one should offer lotus flowers mixed with ghee, or else <s>kumudinī</s> (night-lotus) flowers.
One desiring to bring down [an enemy]: one should offer peacock flesh mixed with pungent oil—death by treachery occurs.
One should offer betel nut, pungent oil, and iron filings—boils arise all over the body.

children.text: kṣīripattrabilvapattrahomena śāntir bhavati /
children.translated_text: By oblation of <s>kṣīri</s> (milky tree) leaves and <s>bilva</s> leaves, pacification occurs.

children.text: tilasamidhaḥ sakaṭutailā hunet tena vidveṣaṇaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: One should offer <s>tila</s> (sesame) sticks with pungent oil—by that, enmity [between others] is created.

children.text: dhattūracūrṇe sāsthicūrṇe sakaṭutailalohacūrṇe ca hute śīghraṃ śatrunāśo bhavati /
children.translated_text: When <s>dhattūra</s> (thorn-apple) powder, bone powder, pungent oil, and iron filings are offered, the swift destruction of enemies occurs.

children.text: mahāmāṃsaṃ saghṛtaṃ hunet mano'bhīṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ bhavati // UT_13.16
children.translated_text: One should offer great flesh with ghee—all that the mind desires comes to pass. // UT 13.16

body.translated_text: <s>Uḍḍāmareśvaratantra</s>, Thirteenth Chapter. <s>Oṃ drīṃ vidyāstambhini stambhini chaḥ chaḥ svāhā</s>. One should first recite this <s>mantra</s> ten thousand times, then meditate upon it mentally. Even in the midst of a forest, one obtains food. <s>Oṃ hauṃ namo bhagavate Mahārudrāya Uḍḍāmareśvarāya huṃ huṃ chaṃ chaṃ drīṃ drīṃ svāhā</s>. With this <s>mantra</s>, for the purpose of <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecrated bathing), one should prepare a <s>kalaśa</s> (ritual pot) consecrated a thousand times with water. Placing the five gems inside it, wrapping it with white cloth, filled with various finely powdered fruits and adorned with various gems—holding the <s>kalaśa</s> at the entrance of the dwelling, at night, together with a woman, one should go to a cremation ground, a great tree, a single tree, a riverbank, a river flowing to the ocean, or a crossroads. Then, having brought the <s>kalaśa</s>, a woman who is barren, whose children have died, who is unfortunate, who has had only one child, or who is crippled—[she] becomes dear to all people; the afflicted one should be massaged.

body.text:
Uḍḍāmareśvaratantra, Caturdaśaḥ paṭalaḥ
klīṃ kāmāture kāmamekhale viṣayiṇi vararati bhagavati amukaṃ me vaśaṃ kuru vaśaṃ kuru klīṃ namaḥ svāhā /
anena mantreṇa bhojanakāle saptagrāsān saptavārābhimantritān bhuñjīta /
saptame divase strī vā puruṣo vā vaśībhavati svaṃ ca dadāti /

children.text: oṃ huṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ huṃ svāhā</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ japet śatrunāśo bhavati /
children.translated_text: One should recite this <s>mantra</s> at the three <s>sandhyās</s> (junctures of the day)—destruction of enemies occurs.

children.text: klīṃ kāli kāli mahākāli kole kinyā svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Klīṃ kāli kāli mahākāli kole kinyā svāhā</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ pūrvam ayutaṃ japtvā saṃdhyākāle sahasraikaṃ homayet tataḥ kaṅkālī varadā bhavati suvarṇacatuṣṭayaṃ pratyahaṃ dadāti // UT_14.1
children.translated_text: Having first recited this <s>mantra</s> ten thousand times, one should offer one thousand oblations at the <s>sandhyā</s> time—then <s>Kaṅkālī</s> becomes the bestower of boons and gives four [pieces of] gold daily. // UT 14.1

children.text: oṃ drīṃ drīṃ draṃ draiṃ drauṃ draḥ huṃ namaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ drīṃ drīṃ draṃ draiṃ drauṃ draḥ huṃ namaḥ svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa pūrvam evāyutaṃ japtvā kevalam ājyaṃ hunet asmād ākarṣaṇaṃ bhavati // UT_14.2
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, having first recited ten thousand times as before, one should offer only ghee—from this, attraction occurs. // UT 14.2

children.text: oṃ drauṃ drauṃ hīṃ hīṃ huṃ namaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ drauṃ drauṃ hīṃ hīṃ huṃ namaḥ svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa pūrvavidhinā japtvārdhamāsād ākarṣaṇaṃ bhavati // UT_14.3
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, having recited according to the previous method, within a fortnight attraction occurs. // UT 14.3

children.text: oṃ haṃ oṃ hūṃ hūṃ hīṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ haṃ oṃ hūṃ hūṃ hīṃ svāhā</s>.

children.text: iti pūrvakhaṅgabhedaḥ // UT_14.4
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the previous <s>khaṅga</s>-division (sword section). // UT 14.4

children.text: sarvasaṃjīvanīmantraḥ oṃ huṃ drīṃ draṃ drauṃ draḥ huṃ huṃ /
children.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> for reviving all: <s>Oṃ huṃ drīṃ draṃ drauṃ draḥ huṃ huṃ</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa sarvajvaranāśanaṃ bhavati // UT_14.5
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, the destruction of all fevers occurs. // UT 14.5

children.text: dīṃ haṃ sini svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Dīṃ haṃ sini svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa sarvajanavaśīkaraṇam // UT_14.6
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, subjugation of all people [is achieved]. // UT 14.6

children.text: oṃ hīṃ namaḥ hīṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hīṃ namaḥ hīṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ sādhyanāmnāyutaṃ japet śavāsanasthito hṛdayaṃ na prakāśayet [... au4 Zeichenjh] amukīṃ tāṃ [... au4 Zeichenjh] saṃgṛhya guṭikāṃ kṛtvā mukhe prakṣipya vidyādharatvaṃ bhavati // UT_14.7
children.translated_text: One should recite this <s>mantra</s> ten thousand times in the name of the target while seated on a corpse; one should not reveal [this to] the heart [...] having gathered [the substance] of that [target woman], having made a pill and placed it in the mouth, one attains the state of a <s>vidyādhara</s> (knowledge-bearing celestial being). // UT 14.7

children.text: oṃ hīṃ huṃ namaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hīṃ huṃ namaḥ</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ pūrvavidhinā japet pādukāsiddhir bhavati // UT_14.8
children.translated_text: One should recite this <s>mantra</s> according to the previous method—<s>pādukā</s>-<s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment of flying sandals) is attained. // UT 14.8

children.text: oṃ kṣaṃ kṣaṃ hrīṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ kṣaṃ kṣaṃ hrīṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ pūrvakrameṇa japed vetālasiddhir bhavati // UT_14.9
children.translated_text: One should recite this <s>mantra</s> according to the previous procedure—<s>vetāla</s>-<s>siddhi</s> (mastery over vampiric spirits) is attained. // UT 14.9

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa narakapālaṃ gṛhītvā tasmin naratailaṃ dattvā tasmin vāyasacakṣuḥsaṃvardhinīṃ vartikāṃ prajvālayet kṛṣṇapakṣāmāvāsyāyāṃ śanivāre andhakūpe śmaśāne vā śūnyāyatane vā kajjalaṃ pātayitavyaṃ tāvat kālaṃ pūrvoktaṃ mantraṃ japet yāvatā kālena vartiśeṣaṃ prajvalati avasāne prabhūtabalidānaṃ kartavyaṃ tatra balistambham ādāya tena siddhāñjanenāñjitanayanaḥ surāsurair api na dṛśyate 'nyalokasya kā kathā // UT_14.10
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, one should take a human skull, place human oil in it, and in it light a wick made of crow's-eye plant. On the <s>Amāvāsyā</s> (new moon) of <s>Kṛṣṇapakṣa</s> (dark fortnight), on a Saturday, in a dark well, a cremation ground, or an empty abode, one should collect the lampblack, reciting the aforementioned <s>mantra</s> for the duration until the remainder of the wick burns out. At the conclusion, a great offering of <s>bali</s> (food oblation) should be made. Having taken the lampblack pillar there, one whose eyes are anointed with that perfected collyrium becomes invisible even to gods and demons—what then to speak of other beings? // UT 14.10

children.text:
oṃ hraṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hraḥ hrīṃ hrīṃ iti śaṅkhinīvidyā /
oṃ hīṃ huṃ iti puṣpāñjalivedhaḥ /
huṃ huṃ iti huṃkāravedhaḥ /
oṃ hrīṃ huṃ ity ālayavedhaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Oṃ hraṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hraḥ hrīṃ hrīṃ</s>—thus is the <s>Śaṅkhinī-vidyā</s> (conch-goddess knowledge).
<s>Oṃ hīṃ huṃ</s>—thus is the <s>puṣpāñjali-vedha</s> (flower-offering piercing).
<s>Huṃ huṃ</s>—thus is the <s>huṃkāra-vedha</s> (huṃ-syllable piercing).
<s>Oṃ hrīṃ huṃ</s>—thus is the <s>ālaya-vedha</s> (abode piercing).

children.text: hrāṃ śivāvedhamantraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Hrāṃ</s>—the piercing <s>mantra</s> of <s>Śivā</s>.

children.text: hrīṃ iti bhramarāvartasaṃghaṭṭavedhaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Hrīṃ</s>—thus is the <s>bhramarāvarta-saṃghaṭṭa-vedha</s> (bee-whirl collision piercing).

children.text: oṃ drīṃ huṃ chaḥ chaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ drīṃ huṃ chaḥ chaḥ svāhā</s>.

children.text: lohatriśūlaṃ kṛtvā rudhireṇa viṣaṃ piṣṭvā tena triśūlaṃ liptvāyutenābhimantritaṃ kṛtvā yasya nāmnā bhūmau nikhanet tasya śīghraṃ mṛtyur bhavati // UT_14.11
children.translated_text: Having made an iron trident, grinding poison with blood, smearing the trident with it and consecrating it ten thousand times—when one buries it in the ground in someone's name, swift death befalls that person. // UT 14.11

children.text: oṃ hrīṃkāri hūṃkāri kapāli samāvedhaṃ bandhuṃ napuṃsakaṃ mahāśaye abhayaṃkari amarākhyaṃ kuru kuru jvaraṃ hana hana ākrośāt kolāhalaṃ parāṃ śaktyākarṣiṇīṃ sarvaśaktiprasaṅginīṃ śāntike huṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃkāri hūṃkāri kapāli samāvedhaṃ bandhuṃ napuṃsakaṃ mahāśaye abhayaṃkari amarākhyaṃ kuru kuru jvaraṃ hana hana ākrośāt kolāhalaṃ parāṃ śaktyākarṣiṇīṃ sarvaśaktiprasaṅginīṃ śāntike huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: imāṃ mahāvidyāṃ śatruvaśaṃkarīṃ manasā smaret sa sarvatra nirbhayo bhavati // UT_14.12
children.translated_text: One who mentally recollects this great <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge-spell), which subjugates enemies, becomes fearless everywhere. // UT 14.12

children.text: oṃ oṃ oṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ sāṃ sāṃ sāṃ sāṃ imaṃ mantraṃ japitvā sthāvarajaṅgamaviṣanāśanaṃ bhavati // UT_14.13
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ oṃ oṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ sāṃ sāṃ sāṃ sāṃ</s>—having recited this <s>mantra</s>, the destruction of all stationary and mobile poisons occurs. // UT 14.13

children.text: oṃ asthi yaṃsthi vidrānidrā saṃnividyā rā ṭaṃ ṭīṃ drīṃ samāsaṃ maṭaṃṭīṃ chaṃ chaṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ asthi yaṃsthi vidrānidrā saṃnividyā rā ṭaṃ ṭīṃ drīṃ samāsaṃ maṭaṃṭīṃ chaṃ chaṃ</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa kākapakṣaṃ sahasraikaṃ hunet yasya nāmnā tam uccāṭayati // UT_14.14
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, one should offer crow's feathers a thousand and one times—whomever's name is [uttered], that person is expelled. // UT 14.14

children.text: strīṃ haṃ anena mantreṇāyute japte sati kavitvavidyā bhavati strīmaṇiśakunavidyāṃ hi saṃjapet jhaṭiti kavitvaṃ karoti // UT_14.15
children.translated_text: <s>Strīṃ haṃ</s>—with this <s>mantra</s>, when ten thousand recitations are performed, the knowledge of poetry arises. One should recite the <s>strīmaṇiśakuna-vidyā</s> (knowledge of women, jewels, and omens)—instantly it produces poetic ability. // UT 14.15

children.text: haṃ aiṃ haṃ haṃ aiṃ vada vada vāgvādini svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Haṃ aiṃ haṃ haṃ aiṃ vada vada vāgvādini svāhā</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ saptavāraṃ japtvādhikādhikaṃ kavitvaṃ ca karoti // UT_14.16
children.translated_text: Having recited this <s>mantra</s> seven times, it produces ever-increasing poetic ability. // UT 14.16

children.text:
oṃ haṃ chaṃ chaṃ chaṃ aiṃ namaḥ svāhā /
sahasrajapādadhikādhikaṃ kavitvado 'yaṃ mantraḥ /
oṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ caṃ chaṃ chaṃ avilambaṃ vaktuḥ stambhayati vācam ālokanāt /
children.translated_text:
<s>Oṃ haṃ chaṃ chaṃ chaṃ aiṃ namaḥ svāhā</s>.
By a thousand recitations, this <s>mantra</s> bestows ever-increasing poetic ability.
<s>Oṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ caṃ chaṃ chaṃ</s>—it instantly paralyzes the speech of a speaker by [mere] glancing.

children.text: huṃ huṃ huṃ huṃ khaṃ khaṃ khaṃ khaṃ chaṃ chaṃ vācāṃ stambhinī vāyusaṃjīvanī vidyā /
children.translated_text: <s>Huṃ huṃ huṃ huṃ khaṃ khaṃ khaṃ khaṃ chaṃ chaṃ</s>—the <s>vidyā</s> that paralyzes speech and revives the breath.

children.text: drīṃ ālokavedhaḥ parokṣavedhaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Drīṃ</s>—the piercing by sight, the piercing from afar.

children.text: hrīṃ sarvavedhanamantraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Hrīṃ</s>—the <s>mantra</s> for piercing everything.

children.text: draṃ drauṃ drauṃ drauṃ draṃ amukaṃ bheji bheji hrīṃ chaṃ chaṃ chaṃ iti visphoṭakasaṃjīvinī avalokanāt kāryasiddhikarī // UT_14.17
children.translated_text: <s>Draṃ drauṃ drauṃ drauṃ draṃ</s> [name] <s>bheji bheji hrīṃ chaṃ chaṃ chaṃ</s>—thus is the spell that produces boils, which accomplishes its purpose by [mere] glancing. // UT 14.17

children.text: oṃ drāṃ drīṃ pūrvarākṣasān nāśaya sarvāṇi bhañjaya saṃtuṣṭā mohaya mahāsvane huṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā iti sarvabhūtamāraṇamantraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ drāṃ drīṃ</s> destroy the former <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), shatter everything, O satisfied one, delude, O great-voiced one, <s>huṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>—thus is the <s>mantra</s> for slaying all <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits).

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ saḥ drāṃ chaḥ chaḥ chaḥ dūrvākṣīrahomena sarvaśāntikarī vidyā // UT_14.18
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ saḥ drāṃ chaḥ chaḥ chaḥ</s>—by oblation of <s>dūrvā</s> (sacred grass) with milk, this <s>vidyā</s> brings about all pacification. // UT 14.18

children.text: huṃ pañcāṇḍaṃ cāṇḍaṃ drīṃ phaṭ svāhā anena mantreṇa manuṣyāsthikīlakaṃ saptāṅgulaṃ sahasradhābhimantritaṃ yasya gehe nikhanet tasya kūṭam utsādinaṃ bhavati uddhṛte sati punaḥ svāsthyaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: <s>Huṃ pañcāṇḍaṃ cāṇḍaṃ drīṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>—with this <s>mantra</s>, a peg made of human bone, seven finger-lengths, consecrated a thousand times—when buried in someone's house, a terrible calamity befalls that person; upon removal, well-being is restored.

children.text: huṃ kṣaṃ amukaṃ phaṭ svāhā anena mantreṇa pecakapakṣimāṃsaṃ kaṭutailena saṃyutaṃ homayet sahasrahomena śatruṃ nipātayati // UT_14.19
children.translated_text: <s>Huṃ kṣaṃ</s> [name] <s>phaṭ svāhā</s>—with this <s>mantra</s>, one should offer owl flesh mixed with pungent oil; by a thousand oblations, one brings down the enemy. // UT 14.19

children.text: oṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ dhuṃ dhuṃ haṃ haḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ dhuṃ dhuṃ haṃ haḥ svāhā</s>.

children.text: iyaṃ hi trailokyavijayānamnī vidyā /
children.translated_text: This indeed is the <s>vidyā</s> named <s>Trailokyavijayā</s> (Conqueror of the Three Worlds).

children.text: manasā smaret sarvakāmaprado 'yaṃ mantraḥ // UT_14.20
children.translated_text: One who mentally recollects [it]—this <s>mantra</s> grants all desires. // UT 14.20

children.text: oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ viśvarūpiṇi piśācini bhūtabhaviṣyādikaṃ vada vada me karṇe kathaya kathaya huṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ viśvarūpiṇi piśācini bhūtabhaviṣyādikaṃ vada vada me karṇe kathaya kathaya huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ śuklapratipadam ārabhya pūrṇimāparyantaṃ sahasraikaṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ japet pratyahaṃ pūtaṃ jalaṃ saghṛtaṃ bhaktapiṇḍaṃ harmyopari rātrau dadyāt trailokye yādṛśī tādṛśī vārttā sādhakasya karṇe bhūtabhaviṣyādikaṃ ca kathayati // UT_14.21
children.translated_text: One should recite this <s>mantra</s> a thousand and one times at the three <s>sandhyās</s> daily, beginning from the bright <s>pratipada</s> (first lunar day) until the full moon. Daily, one should place purified water and a ball of food mixed with ghee on a rooftop at night—[a spirit] tells the practitioner about all affairs of the three worlds, past, future, and so on, in his ear. // UT 14.21

children.text: oṃ raṃ rāṃ saṃ sāṃ laṃ lāṃ haṃ haḥ saṃ saḥ khaṃ khaḥ taṃ taḥ dhaṃ saṃ sphuṃ sphaḥ hrīṃ huṃ huṃ huṃ kṣīṃ kṣīṃ kṣauṃ sauṃ saḥ chaṃ chaḥ dhaṃ saḥ sphuṃ sphaḥ hrīṃ huṃ huṃ huṃ kṣīṃ kṣīṃ kṣauṃ saṃ phaṃ phaḥ huṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ raṃ rāṃ saṃ sāṃ laṃ lāṃ haṃ haḥ saṃ saḥ khaṃ khaḥ taṃ taḥ dhaṃ saṃ sphuṃ sphaḥ hrīṃ huṃ huṃ huṃ kṣīṃ kṣīṃ kṣauṃ sauṃ saḥ chaṃ chaḥ dhaṃ saḥ sphuṃ sphaḥ hrīṃ huṃ huṃ huṃ kṣīṃ kṣīṃ kṣauṃ saṃ phaṃ phaḥ huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ samastaviṣanāśanamantraḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the <s>mantra</s> for the destruction of all poisons.

children.text: sacarācare oṃ sacarācare oṃ huṃ huṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ kṣakṣakṣaḥ hasaḥ oṃ saṃ huṃ hrīṃ sarveśa viṣṇubalena śaṃkaradarpeṇa vāyuvegena ravitejasā candrakāntyā vairaṃ bāṇaśūrpaṇaṃ sarvaṃ viṣaharaṃ vada sarvarakṣāṃsi hi nāśaya 2 bhañjaya 2 sarvaduṣṭān mohaya 2 deva huṃ phaṭ svāhā huṃ phaṭ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Sacarācare oṃ sacarācare oṃ huṃ huṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ kṣakṣakṣaḥ hasaḥ oṃ saṃ huṃ hrīṃ sarveśa</s>—by the power of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, by the pride of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, by the speed of <s>Vāyu</s>, by the brilliance of <s>Ravi</s> (the Sun), by the beauty of <s>Candra</s> (the Moon), declare all poison to be destroyed—the arrows and winnowing fan of <s>Vaira</s>—destroy all <s>rakṣas</s> (demons), destroy, shatter, shatter, delude all the wicked, delude, O God, <s>huṃ phaṭ svāhā huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

children.text: imaṃ mantram aṣṭottarasahasraṃ śataṃ vā japtvā saptame divase siddhiḥ samākarṣaṇaṃ bhavati // UT_14.22
children.translated_text: Having recited this <s>mantra</s> one thousand and eight times or a hundred times, on the seventh day, <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) and attraction are achieved. // UT 14.22

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ amukaṃ chaḥ chaḥ anena mantreṇa mānuṣyāsthimayaṃ kīlakam ekādaśāṅgulaṃ sahasreṇābhimantritaṃ yasya gṛhe nikhanet tasya kūṭaṃ cotsādanaṃ bhavati uddhṛte punaḥ svāsthyaṃ bhavati // UT_14.23
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ</s> [name] <s>chaḥ chaḥ</s>—with this <s>mantra</s>, a peg made of human bone, eleven finger-lengths, consecrated a thousand times—when buried in someone's house, a terrible calamity befalls that person; upon removal, well-being is restored. // UT 14.23

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ kāla kaṅkāla mahākāla karālavadana amukaṃ gṛhṇa triśūlena bhinddhi 2 khaḍgena chinddhi 2 huṃ phaṭ chaḥ chaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ kāla kaṅkāla mahākāla karālavadana</s> [name] <s>gṛhṇa</s> (seize), pierce with the trident, pierce, cut with the sword, cut, <s>huṃ phaṭ chaḥ chaḥ svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa vibhītakakāṣṭhakīlakam ekaviṃśatyaṅgulaṃ sahasreṇābhimantritaṃ yasya gṛhadvāre nikhanyate tasya sadyo dehanipātanaṃ bhavati // UT_14.24
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, a peg made of <s>vibhītaka</s> (Terminalia bellirica) wood, twenty-one finger-lengths, consecrated a thousand times—when buried at the door of someone's house, the immediate destruction of that person's body occurs. // UT 14.24

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ huṃ amukaṃ chaḥ chaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ huṃ</s> [name] <s>chaḥ chaḥ</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa siddhikāṣṭhamayaṃ kīlakaṃ navāṅgulaṃ sahasreṇābhimantritaṃ yasya gṛhe nikhanyate sa vaśyo bhavati /
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, a peg made of <s>siddhi</s>-wood (auspicious wood), nine finger-lengths, consecrated a thousand times—when buried in someone's house, that person comes under one's control.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ mātaṃgini aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ mātaṃgini aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa rājikāṃ lavaṇaghṛtamiśritāṃ yasya nāmnā saha homayet tāṃ striyaṃ puruṣaṃ vā vaśayaty ākarṣaṇaṃ ca karoti // UT_14.25
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, one should offer <s>rājikā</s> (mustard seeds) mixed with salt and ghee in someone's name—it subjugates that woman or man and also effects attraction. // UT 14.25

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ chaḥ chaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ chaḥ chaḥ</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa vāḍavakāṣṭhamayaṃ kīlakaṃ trayodaśāṅgulaṃ sahasreṇābhimantritaṃ yasya gṛhe nikhanet sa cakṣurbhyām andho bhavati // UT_14.26
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, a peg made of <s>vāḍava</s>-wood (submarine fire wood), thirteen finger-lengths, consecrated a thousand times—when buried in someone's house, that person becomes blind in both eyes. // UT 14.26

children.text: oṃ chaḥ oṃ chaḥ chaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ chaḥ oṃ chaḥ chaḥ</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa bilvakāṣṭhasya kīlakaṃ daśāṅgulaṃ sahasreṇābhimantritaṃ yasya gṛhe nikhanet saparivārasya tasya pretatvaṃ bhavati // UT_14.27
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, a peg of <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) wood, ten finger-lengths, consecrated a thousand times—when buried in someone's house, that person together with their family becomes as if dead (ghost-like). // UT 14.27

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ amukīṃ me prayaccha svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ amukīṃ me prayaccha svāhā</s>.

children.text: anena mantreṇa pāṭalākāṣṭhamayaṃ pañcāṅgulaṃ kīlakaṃ sahasreṇābhimantritaṃ yasya nāmnā devatāyatane nikhanet sa śīghraṃ kanyāṃ labhate // UT_14.28
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, a peg made of <s>pāṭalā</s> (Stereospermum) wood, five finger-lengths, consecrated a thousand times—when buried in a temple in someone's name, that person quickly obtains a maiden. // UT 14.28

body.translated_text:
<s>Uḍḍāmareśvaratantra</s>, Fourteenth Chapter.
<s>Klīṃ kāmāture kāmamekhale viṣayiṇi vararati bhagavati amukaṃ me vaśaṃ kuru vaśaṃ kuru klīṃ namaḥ svāhā</s>.
With this <s>mantra</s>, at mealtime, one should eat seven morsels consecrated seven times.
On the seventh day, a woman or a man comes under one's control and gives their own [body].

children.text: ṣaṭkoṇaṃ yantraṃ likhitvā tatra ṣaṭkoṇe oṃ kurukulle svāhā iti mantraṃ pūrvakoṇe likhet /
children.translated_text: Having drawn a hexagonal <s>yantra</s> (mystical diagram), one should write the <s>mantra</s> "<s>Oṃ kurukulle svāhā</s>" in the eastern corner of the hexagon.

children.text: kuru ity akṣaradvayam aparakoṇe likhet /
children.translated_text: The two syllables "<s>kuru</s>" should be written in the other corner.

children.text: akṣaraikaṃ pūrvāvartakrameṇa lekhitavyam /
children.translated_text: Each syllable should be written following the clockwise order.

children.text: tato bhūrjapattre imaṃ mantraṃ likhitvā gṛhadvāre dehalyā ekadeśe dhṛte sati gṛhasarpam uccāṭayati vivaradvāri dhṛte vivarastho naśyaty eva // UT_15.1
children.translated_text: Then, having written this <s>mantra</s> on a birch-bark leaf and placed it at one spot on the threshold of a house door, it expels snakes from the house; when placed at a burrow entrance, the one dwelling in the burrow surely perishes. // UT 15.1

children.text: raktakaravīrapuṣpam āmrapattrabhasmanā liptaṃ tatkṣaṇād eva śubhraṃ bhavati tathā gandhakadhūpenāpi bhāvitena śuktir bhavati /
children.translated_text: A red oleander flower, when smeared with mango-leaf ash, becomes white at that very instant. Likewise, when treated with sulfur-fumigation, it becomes [like] a shell (pearl-white).

children.text: loke hayamāra ityākhyasya raktakaravīrasya puṣpaṃ tūlavartikāgandhakena saha saṃyojya tatkṣaṇād eva jvalati /
children.translated_text: The flower of the red oleander, known in common parlance as "horse-killer" (<s>hayamāra</s>), when combined with cotton-wick and sulfur, ignites at that very instant.

children.text: tathā ṭaṅkanaharidrābhyāṃ kṛte lepe kuṅkumakāntir bhavati // UT_15.2
children.translated_text: Likewise, when a paste is made with borax and turmeric, it acquires the luster of saffron. // UT 15.2

children.text: purāṇaśuṣkagomayaṃ yadā jale pātayet tadā bhīmoṣmaṇā tasmād budbudam utpadyate /
children.translated_text: When old dried cow dung is cast into water, due to intense heat, bubbles arise from it.

children.text: evaṃ gauraṃ tu bhūmyupari bhūtalaṃ spṛṣṭvā raktakaravīravṛkṣo jāyate iti /
children.translated_text: Thus, the white [substance], upon touching the surface of the earth above, a red oleander tree is born—so it is said.

children.text: rūpake tāmre bhramara iva kumbhe samarpayet kiṃcid anuyogitvena mano'nurāgo bhavati tāmbūlarāgataḥ naśyati haridrārāgo ravikiraṇāt // UT_15.3
children.translated_text: In a copper vessel, like a bee [is placed] in a pot, one should offer something as a supplement—mental attachment arises; the betel-stain disappears; turmeric-color vanishes from sunlight. // UT 15.3

children.text: oṃ huṃ sati kurur upakṣiśabdataḥ kuralakuṅkumena iti prasiddhiḥ kroñca ity api tasya nāma jihvākrīṃkṛtaṃ vāmakaratalamadhyalagnaparilepaṃ darśayitvā uditaviśvadhārābhasmanā punar api karatalalagnāt pradarśya gatyāścaryamate śiśudugdhabhāvitāt śodhayitvā gavādidugdhaṃ coṣṇaṃ kāṃsyapātre kṛtvā tīkṣṇataraṃ dhṛtvā taṇḍulanikṣepaṇena kṣīraṃ bhavati // UT_15.4
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ huṃ</s>—<s>sati</s> (thus it is); from the word <s>kurur upakṣi</s>, with saffron-paste, thus is the established [method]; <s>kroñca</s> is also its name. Having shown the tongue made to produce the "<s>krīṃ</s>" sound, with paste applied to the center of the left palm, and then showing again with the ash of universal support applied to the palm, [it appears as] a wonder of movement. Having purified with infant's milk, placing warm cow's milk or similar in a bronze vessel and holding [it] very firmly, by casting rice grains, it becomes [like] milk. // UT 15.4

children.text: bhūrjapattrapuṭakaṃ tilatailena dīpayitvā vividhabhakṣyānnaṃ sādhayet yathā lauhabhājane sādhyate /
children.translated_text: Having lit a birch-bark container with sesame oil, one can cook various foods and dishes just as [they would be] cooked in an iron vessel.

children.text: vārtākarañjikāpalam iti tat sūtreṇa veṣṭayitvā dīpayitvā ca jvālayet tenāvisūtreṇa veṣṭite ca sūtraṃ saṃdahyate vārtākaś ca pacyate // UT_15.5
children.translated_text: The fruit of the <s>vārtāka</s> (eggplant) and <s>karañjikā</s>—having wrapped it with thread and lit it, it burns; with that non-[burning] thread wrapped around it, the thread is consumed while the eggplant is cooked. // UT 15.5

children.text: ādipaṅktau sapta svarān saṃlikhya tadadhaḥpaṅktau kādisaptavargāt saṃlikhya tadadhaḥpaṅktau haridrādikrameṇālekhanīyā tatra svaravarṇayojanena saṃkocanād akṣarakoṣṭhādisaṃsparśanāt saṃjāyate /
children.translated_text: In the first row, having written the seven vowels, in the row below that writing the seven classes beginning with <s>ka</s>, and in the row below that writing in order beginning with turmeric [ink]—by combining vowels and consonants, through contraction and touching of the letter-cells, [the cipher] is produced.

children.text: bahuṣu madhyeṣu dattasaṃjñākṛtasaṃketaś cauraḥ svadṛṣṭim api saptasaptasvarādau jānāti /
children.translated_text: A thief who has given signals and made signs among many [people] in their midst—one identifies [him] through the seven-seven vowel [cipher] system and one's own observation.

children.text: vyāpāramadhye kṣaṇarasikaś cauro jñāyate kṛto bhadradravye // UT_15.6
children.translated_text: In the midst of activities, a thief who is momentarily careless is identified through the use of auspicious objects. // UT 15.6

children.text:
kutrāpi dhattūrakabījaṃ kṣiptvā tad vā bhakṣati tadā tadguṇādiphalaṃ labhyate asau cauraḥ iti /
svalpacaracaurās tu vastulābhe pradātāraḥ /
children.translated_text:
If one casts <s>dhattūra</s> (thorn-apple) seeds somewhere and [the suspect] eats them, then the characteristic effects of that [plant] are obtained—[thus] "this is the thief."
Petty thieves, upon obtaining goods, become givers [i.e., reveal themselves].

children.text: kṣīryarkādivṛkṣadugdhena saṃlikhitaṃ cauranāmākṣaraṃ karatale 'pi likhitam anantaraṃ bhūrjapattre kṛtam api mardane sparśayitvā bhakṣituṃ tato dadāti aparilikhitaṃ cauranāma pattrayuktaṃ ca arigṛhagarbhamṛttikākāṇḍakaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: The letters of the thief's name, written with the milk of <s>arka</s> (milkweed) and similar milk-trees, even when written on the palm, then also made on birch-bark, by pressing and touching [the suspect] to eat [the writing]—then the thief's name, not [visibly] written, together with the leaf, and a ball of clay from the interior of the enemy's house, is [prepared].

children.text: jale sādhunāma pattrayuktamṛttikā ca jale majjati tataḥ spṛṣṭvā kriyate asau cauraḥ iti /
children.translated_text: In water, a clay ball with a good person's name and leaf sinks in the water; then by touching [the suspect], it is established—"this is the thief."

children.text: kṣīritarudugdhalikhitakṣudralekhe aṅgāracūrṇena marditāḥ spaṣṭā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Letters finely written with the milk of the milkweed tree, when rubbed with charcoal powder, become clearly visible.

children.text: kūṭo 'pi viparītalikhitavarṇa ādarśādau pratikṛtibhāvāpanno varṇavaiparītyāt prativivardhitanyāsaḥ atidṛḍhā masī bhavati // UT_15.7
children.translated_text: A secret [message] with letters written in reverse—when reflected in a mirror and such, the reversal of letters is recognized; with reversed inscription, the ink becomes extremely firm. // UT 15.7

children.text:
nimbatālake samatāmrabhājane yāmamātramarditena vidhir astu samabhāgatā yathā āmalakīharītakīvibhītakanimbakhādirāṇām nīrākhyārājakaravīrarasaiḥ samastarasakajjalamuktamardanaprakāreṇa yāmamātreṇa pratyekaṃ yena prakāreṇa masidravyaṃ jāyate /
śirīṣavṛkṣatvakcūrṇaṃ khadiraṃ vinā tāmbūlarāgaṃ janayati /
children.translated_text:
In a <s>nimba</s> (neem) preparation with an equal [amount in a] copper vessel, the procedure should be [applied] with grinding for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) in equal portions—namely, of <s>āmalakī</s> (Indian gooseberry), <s>harītakī</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>vibhītaka</s> (Terminalia bellirica), neem, and <s>khadira</s> (catechu); with the juices of the plant called <s>nīra</s> and <s>rājakaravīra</s> (king-oleander); by the method of grinding all the juices with lampblack—in one <s>yāma</s> for each, by this method the ink substance is produced.
The bark-powder of the <s>śirīṣa</s> (Albizia) tree, without <s>khadira</s>, produces a betel-like red color.

children.text: tiryaka bhūmau nārikelaphalam asthisahitaṃ mukhena karṇikāyām ekena prahāreṇa dvidhā bhavati /
children.translated_text: A coconut with its shell, [placed] horizontally on the ground with its mouth at the eye [of the fruit], splits into two with a single blow.

children.text: laghukāṣṭhasūkṣmaracitapākāṃ vinā pādaikaṃ vā bhramati /
children.translated_text: Without [visible support], a light wooden [top] finely crafted spins on one foot alone.

children.text: guñjāphalāsthiliptaṃ stambhitaṃ taduttarapādaṃ prayojya prapadātyantaṃ bhramati tadā pādatale tālakāralagnā uttiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: Smeared with <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea) seed paste, having fixed that upper foot and applied [force] to the very tip of the forefoot, it spins exceedingly—then at the sole of the foot, the smeared substance rises up.

children.text: evaṃ laghukāṣṭhanirmitāsamakaḥ pāpapurahāsārthaṃ dattamukhaveṣṭaṃ kiṃcit yas tena sitavastrādau kaṭyāṃ lagnam upatiṣṭhamānās tiṣṭhati // UT_15.8
