children.translated_text: Thus a top made of light wood, with a covering placed on the mouth for the purpose of amusing wicked [audiences], with something [attached] at the waist to a white cloth, remains standing upright. // UT 15.8

children.text: evaṃ niviḍāmbarapihitajambādau adhomukhakāṃsyabhājananihitam aṅgāraṃ na dahati vastraṃ dahati cāpi śiśirajalamiśritam api ānataphalacūrṇabhāvitakalaśaḥ tīkṣṇaś ca kāṃsyabhājananihitaṃ guruḍḍanāpy aśaktaṃ na bhavati tadānīṃ tiktaṃ yāti yac chuktaṃ miṣṭam eti kajjalacavikācūrṇābhyāṃ kramasaṃlikhitapustakamadhyakāraṇe 'pi yatheṣṭayā pacyate yathā kaṭāhe ramyatare madhunāgniprajvalite sakuṇḍādau jalapūrṇe adhomukhe ujjvalaṃ svayam eti dhūmābhyāṃ svayam udgirati vartidvaye śaśaviṣṭhāpūrṇagarbhe kamaṭhair adhovartiviṣṭhāyitāpi upari jvalajjvālājvalitavartijvālām api jvalitadhūmam aṅgāratīkṣṇaśikhayā nāḍikādau /
children.translated_text: Thus, in a <s>jāmba</s> (rose-apple) vessel and the like covered with thick cloth, a charcoal placed inside a face-down bronze vessel does not burn the cloth, yet also burns; even when mixed with cold water, a pot treated with <s>ānata</s>-fruit powder [remains] sharp; even a heavy weight placed in the bronze vessel does not become weakened. At that time, what is bitter becomes astringent, what is sour becomes sweet. With lampblack and <s>cavikā</s> (a pungent spice) powder written in sequence inside a book, [food] is cooked as desired—as in a beautiful cauldron ignited by honey-fire, with a <s>kuṇḍa</s> (fire-pit) and other [vessels] filled with water facing downward, it blazes on its own and emits smoke on its own; with two wicks whose cores are filled with rabbit droppings, even with excrement placed below, the wick-flame blazes above, burning with smoke and the sharp tip of charcoal-flame in a tube and so forth.

children.text: vālivāte 'yaṃ prayogaḥ kāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: This procedure should be performed in a sand-wind [demonstration].

children.text: vāmakarāṅguliparyantaṃ gopitaṃ sūtracihnam apy acihnaṃ ca dṛśyate janasya viṣamasamākṣareṇa vīkṣite kālaḥ asamam api puruṣaṃ jānīyāt /
children.translated_text: A thread-mark concealed up to the fingers of the left hand—even the invisible [mark] becomes visible to people; by viewing with uneven-numbered syllables, one determines the time; even an unequal person can be identified.

children.text: pañcadāḍime śikhare masiguṇite yaddhi bhavati tāvat guṭike vijānīyāt /
children.translated_text: On five pomegranates, at the tip, marked with ink—one should know as many pills [as correspond to the marks].

children.text: akālavakre sati kālam atha phalacūrṇena militvā bhasmanā saha ghṛtena kākañjikā sahasā bhavati // UT_15.9
children.translated_text: When there is an untimely curve, then [one determines] the time; having mixed with fruit-powder and ash together with ghee, <s>kākañjikā</s> (a sour preparation) is instantly produced. // UT 15.9

children.text: agādhasthirajale dhūmacūrṇena likhitacintādi bhītavad bhāṣate na nimajjatīti /
children.translated_text: In deep, still water, [an object] inscribed with smoke-powder, like an anxious [living thing], speaks—it does not sink.

children.text: samadaśaghṛtajadhṛtasamāveśārdhaṃ dhṛtamūṣalaṃ tiṣṭhati // UT_15.10
children.translated_text: An equal ten-[part] ghee-held balanced half-immersed pestle stands [upright]. // UT 15.10

children.text:
puṣyanakṣatre kuṅkumāvartitena bāṇena dūrastham api lakṣyaṃ bālo 'pi vidhyate /
ṣaṇḍaṃ gomayānāṃ vartidīpakāntyā dagdhaṃ madhye hataśaśarudhiraṃ dṛśyate tatrāpi tailaṃ yat kiṃcid iti /
children.translated_text:
Under the <s>Puṣya nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion), with an arrow coated in saffron, even a child can hit a distant target.
A heap of cow-dung [cakes]—by the light of a wick-lamp, when burned, the blood of a slain rabbit is seen in the middle; there is also some oil in that.

children.text: śvetārkaphale tūlakaṃ sarṣapasamaṃ tailenaikīkṛtavartikadīpajvālāyāṃ gṛhoparivaṃśādidāru sarvaṃ sarpa iva dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: In the cotton of a white <s>arka</s> (milkweed) fruit, [making] a wick equal to a mustard seed unified with oil—in the flame of the wick-lamp, all the wood such as bamboo above the house appears as serpents.

children.text: bhujagataile sacchidrabhāṇḍe bhujaṃgaṃ kṣiptvā acchidrabhāṇḍāntare vyavasthitam agnipātena jalaṃ jvalati /
children.translated_text: Having placed a snake into a vessel with holes [filled with] snake-oil, and [then] placed within a vessel without holes—by applying fire, the water blazes.

children.text: tadaiva tailaṃ pūrvaprakāreṇa kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ maṇḍūkatailāṅkitena sarvaṃ śātrava sarvaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: At that very time, with oil in the previous manner, on <s>Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī</s> (the dark eighth lunar day), everything marked with frog-oil—all enemies are [destroyed].

children.text: dīpakāntyā dīpayitvā yat kiṃcic ca kukkuṭapakṣicañcvādividagdhanālalakṣitā satī hṛtā lekhā yadāyāti harikapālaṃ dhṛtvā bhavati tadā taj jalapūrṇāṃ ca kalaśaṃ riktakaṃ bhavati tathā maricaśuṇṭhī pippalīcūrṇenobhābhyāṃ vāmacaraṇatalaṃ liptvā tenāhato vṛkṣaḥ kalpavṛkṣaś ca nameruphalaṃ prasūyate // UT_15.11
children.translated_text: By lighting with a lamp-flame, whatever [is prepared with] chicken feathers and beak-burnt-stalk marks, when brought, when a line comes, having held a monkey's skull—then that water-filled pot becomes empty. Likewise, having smeared the sole of the left foot with the powder of pepper, dry ginger, and long pepper, a tree struck by that [foot] becomes a wish-fulfilling tree and bears <s>nameru</s> (Eugenia) fruit. // UT 15.11

children.text: kṛṣṇā gauḥ prasavakāle tadvat samānavarṇaṃ jarāyur āgatatvena prajāreṇḍalā phalaṃ dṛṣṭvā muṣṭigṛhīte uccais tamasi phalaṃ prāyeṇa kṛtvā pradāsyati tathā kālāyitamudrikā varagostanī syād āpatitā gṛhītā nikṣiptā tu aṣṭau pūrvaphalāni janayati /
children.translated_text: A black cow, at the time of calving, when a placenta of the same color comes forth, having seen the <s>prajāreṇḍalā</s> fruit and grasped it in the fist, aloft in darkness—[she] will mostly produce fruit and give it; likewise, a darkened ring, being an excellent cow-teat, when fallen and grasped and deposited, produces eight of the aforementioned fruits.

children.text: samustāharitālamanaḥśilābhyāṃ navanītādiyogena kāritāñjane mayūrasya viṣṭhayā kṛtvā hastaṃ limpet tatra sthitaṃ dravyaṃ brahmāpi na paśyati /
children.translated_text: Having made a collyrium with <s>mustā</s> (nut grass), <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment), and <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) combined with butter and similar substances, having applied it to the hand with peacock droppings—the substance placed there, even <s>Brahmā</s> cannot see.

children.text: samukhaṃ phalacūrṇaṃ miśrodvartanakājale kṣiptvā krimisahasratulyaṃ dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Having cast face-up fruit-powder mixed into <s>udvartana</s> (rubbing) water, it appears like a thousand worms.

children.text: hayakālīyakasya śoṣitasya cūrṇaṃ gavaśīrṣakeṇa samudvartanena tātkālikaṃ sūkṣmajale niḥkṣipya sabījaṃ kṛṣir uccalati // UT_15.12
children.translated_text: The powder of dried <s>hayakālīyaka</s> (a plant), by rubbing with <s>gavaśīrṣaka</s> (a mineral), immediately casting it into fine water—seeded crops spring up. // UT 15.12

children.text:
adhaḥpaṭenāśasyāvaśyādi dṛṣṭvā pādāgrasthitaṃ dravyaṃ dṛśyate /
japākusumodvartitāṅgaṃ churikādau kaṇācitaikakīṭakāphalākhyā yantrite rudhiravaj jaḍitaṃ kṣīrivṛkṣatvagavabhāvitā tailāktā vastravartir jalair jvalati /
children.translated_text:
By [looking through] a cloth below, having seen unhusked grain and the like, the object placed at the tip of the foot becomes visible.
A body rubbed with <s>japā</s> (hibiscus) flowers, [when applied to] a knife and such with scattered grains—the fruit called <s>ekakīṭakā</s>—in the device, it becomes congealed like blood. A wick made of cloth soaked in milkweed-bark and anointed with oil burns in water.

children.text: evaṃ samudratailayuktāpi vartikā jvalati /
children.translated_text: Likewise, a wick combined with ocean-oil also burns [in water].

children.text: droṇakapuṣpādīni kṣudrapuṣpāṇi cūrṇāgre viniṣkṣipya dhattūrabījāni jalasiktāni sajīvavat phalanti /
children.translated_text: Having cast small flowers such as <s>droṇaka</s> (Leucas) flowers at the tip of the powder, <s>dhattūra</s> seeds sprinkled with water sprout as if alive.

children.text: ikṣuḥ kukkuṭībījacūrṇena sudarśanapattram iva tatkṣaṇāt jāyate /
children.translated_text: Sugarcane, with chicken-egg powder, produces a <s>sudarśana</s> (Chrysanthemum) leaf-like [growth] at that very instant.

children.text: masṛṇakarpaṭaṃ nirmalakāṃsyabhājane 'rkasammukhaṃ sthāpanena vartulakayogād agnir uttarati // UT_15.13
children.translated_text: By placing a smooth cloth in a clean bronze vessel facing the sun, through the application of a circular [lens], fire rises up. // UT 15.13
